The Require multifactor authentication grant control
The Require app protection policy grant control
A sign-in frequency session control of one hour
questions.explain: Authentication strengths limit which method combinations satisfy a policy; the Phishing-resistant MFA strength allows only those methods. Plain Require MFA accepts any MFA method, including SMS. App protection policy and sign-in frequency don't restrict the authentication method type.

questions.stem: For each statement about multifactor authentication, select Yes if true.

statements.s: An MFA fatigue attack floods a user with push prompts hoping the user approves one.
Microsoft Entra ID provides the built-in authentication strengths MFA, Passwordless MFA and Phishing-resistant MFA.
Administrators can't create custom authentication strengths in Microsoft Entra ID.

questions.explain: MFA fatigue relies on repeated push prompts, which number matching helps defeat. Entra ID has three built-in strengths and also lets Conditional Access administrators create custom authentication strengths.

questions.stem: A small organization has only Microsoft Entra ID Free licences and wants a baseline that requires users to register for MFA and blocks legacy authentication. What should it use?
options: Microsoft Entra ID Protection risk policies
questions.explain: Security defaults are free and enforce MFA registration, MFA for admins and blocking of legacy authentication. Conditional Access needs P1, while ID Protection risk policies and PIM need P2 or ID Governance.

questions.stem: For each statement about security defaults, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Security defaults block authentication requests that use legacy authentication protocols.
You can keep security defaults enabled and add Conditional Access policies to exclude specific users.
Security defaults require MFA when administrators access the Azure portal and Azure CLI.

questions.explain: Security defaults block legacy authentication and protect privileged activities such as the Azure portal, Azure PowerShell and Azure CLI. They can't be combined with Conditional Access and have no exclusions; to customise you must disable them and use Conditional Access.

questions.case: Northwind has security defaults enabled. It has just bought Microsoft Entra ID P1 licences. The security team wants to require MFA only when users sign in from outside two office IP ranges, and to exclude two emergency access accounts from MFA prompts.
questions.stem: What should the team do?
options: Add the office IP ranges as exclusions in security defaults
Disable security defaults and create Conditional Access policies using named locations
Keep security defaults and create an ID Protection sign-in risk policy
Enable per-user MFA on top of security defaults for the excluded accounts
questions.explain: Security defaults can't be customised with locations or exclusions and can't run alongside Conditional Access. Northwind must turn them off and build Conditional Access policies with named locations and excluded accounts. Risk policies need P2 and don't meet the location need.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Entra feature lets users who forgot their password reset it themselves after verifying their identity with registered methods?
questions.explain: SSPR lets users reset or unlock their own accounts after verifying with one or two methods. PHS syncs password hashes to the cloud, Password Protection blocks weak passwords, and smart lockout locks out attackers guessing passwords.

questions.stem: Users are synchronized from AD DS. After enabling SSPR, a user resets her password in the cloud, but the new password doesn't work when she signs in to her domain-joined PC. What must be enabled?
questions.explain: Password writeback sends passwords reset in the cloud back to on-premises AD DS so hybrid users can use them everywhere. Seamless SSO reduces prompts but doesn't sync passwords. Banned lists and combined registration don't write passwords back.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about self-service password reset are correct? Select TWO.
options: Administrators can require users to verify with either one or two methods to reset a password
SSPR password reset for cloud users is included with Microsoft Entra ID Free
Accounts in administrator roles are subject to a stronger two-gate reset policy
SSPR lets users reset passwords without registering any authentication methods
SSPR replaces the need for multifactor authentication
questions.explain: Admins choose one or two required methods, and admin accounts get a stricter two-gate policy. Password reset needs P1/P2 or eligible Microsoft 365 plans (Free covers only password change). Users must register methods first, and SSPR doesn't replace MFA.

questions.stem: Contoso wants to stop users from choosing passwords that contain the word 'contoso' or its product names. What should it configure?
options: A custom banned password list in Microsoft Entra Password Protection
A Conditional Access require password change control
questions.explain: The custom banned password list holds organization-specific terms such as brand and product names. The global list is maintained by Microsoft and can't be edited. Smart lockout limits guessing, and the password change control doesn't check password content.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Entra Password Protection and smart lockout, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Administrators can remove entries from the global banned password list.
The custom banned password list can contain up to 1,000 terms.
Smart lockout tries to lock out attackers while letting the genuine user keep signing in from familiar locations.

questions.explain: The global banned password list is maintained by Microsoft and can't be changed or disabled. The custom list holds up to 1,000 base terms. Smart lockout distinguishes familiar from unfamiliar sign-in locations to avoid locking out the real user.

questions.case: Adatum uses Microsoft Entra ID P1 and synchronizes users from AD DS. It already enforces a custom banned password list in the cloud. Auditors found users still set weak passwords such as 'Adatum2026!' when they press Ctrl+Alt+Del on domain-joined PCs to change passwords in AD DS.
questions.stem: What should Adatum deploy to apply the same banned password rules to AD DS password changes?
options: Password writeback in Microsoft Entra Connect
Microsoft Entra Password Protection DC agent and proxy service on-premises
A Conditional Access policy requiring a password change
Self-service password reset for all users
questions.explain: The on-premises Password Protection DC agent, with the proxy service, enforces the global and custom banned lists for AD DS password changes. Writeback only sends cloud resets on-premises. A password change control or SSPR doesn't check passwords changed directly in AD DS.

questions.stem: An attacker repeatedly tries passwords against a user account from an unfamiliar IP address. Which always-on Microsoft Entra ID feature temporarily locks the attacker out?
options: Microsoft Entra ID Protection user risk policy
questions.explain: Smart lockout is always on and locks accounts temporarily after repeated failed sign-ins, aiming at the attacker. Continuous access evaluation revokes existing sessions on critical events. A user risk policy needs P2 and configuration, and number matching applies to Authenticator push.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Entra ID feature evaluates signals such as user, location, device and application to decide whether to allow, block or require MFA for a sign-in?
questions.explain: Conditional Access is the if-then policy engine that combines signals to make access decisions. Connect Health monitors hybrid sync, entitlement management handles access requests, and administrative units limit admin role scope.

questions.stem: Which THREE can be used as conditions or assignments in a Conditional Access policy? Select THREE.
options: Location based on IP address or country/region
The number of groups the user owns
questions.explain: Conditional Access can evaluate sign-in risk (from ID Protection), device platforms and locations such as named IP ranges or countries. Mailbox size and group ownership counts are not Conditional Access signals.

questions.stem: For each statement about Conditional Access, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Conditional Access policies are enforced after first-factor authentication is completed.
If one applicable policy blocks access and another grants it with MFA, the user is granted access after MFA.
Emergency access accounts should usually be excluded from Conditional Access policies to avoid tenant lockout.

questions.explain: Conditional Access runs after the first factor succeeds. When multiple policies apply, all must be satisfied and a Block policy wins. Microsoft recommends excluding break-glass accounts so a misconfigured policy can't lock out all administrators.

questions.case: Woodgrove Bank has employees only in New Zealand and Australia. It has seen password spray attempts against its tenant from other countries. Management wants to stop sign-ins from all other countries while still allowing staff to sign in normally from the two countries. Woodgrove has Microsoft Entra ID P1.
questions.stem: What should the administrator configure?
options: Security defaults with a country exclusion
Smart lockout with a lower threshold
A named location for allowed countries and a Conditional Access policy that blocks all other locations
A custom banned password list containing the attackers' IP addresses
questions.explain: Named locations with country/region selection plus a Block policy for all other locations meet the requirement with P1. Security defaults have no location settings. Smart lockout reduces guessing but doesn't restrict countries, and banned password lists hold password terms, not IP addresses.

questions.stem: A user signs in to a cloud app protected by Conditional Access. Put the steps in order.
options: The user completes first-factor authentication with Microsoft Entra ID
Conditional Access collects signals such as user, location, device and app
Applicable policies are evaluated and a decision is made
The user satisfies required controls such as MFA, or access is blocked
A token is issued and the user reaches the app
questions.explain: Conditional Access is evaluated after first-factor authentication. It gathers signals, evaluates every policy that applies, enforces the resulting controls (or blocks), and only then is a token issued for the app.

questions.stem: What is the minimum Microsoft Entra ID licence required to create Conditional Access policies?
questions.explain: Conditional Access requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 (included in plans such as Microsoft 365 E3 and Business Premium). Free tenants use security defaults. ID Governance is an add-on for governance features, and Workload ID Premium extends policies to workload identities.

questions.stem: Which TWO are session controls, rather than grant controls, in Conditional Access? Select TWO.
options: Require device to be marked as compliant
questions.explain: Sign-in frequency and Conditional Access App Control shape the session after sign-in. Requiring a compliant device, MFA or acceptance of terms of use are grant controls that must be met before access is allowed.

questions.case: Litware lets contractors use unmanaged personal laptops to reach SharePoint Online and other cloud apps. Security wants contractors' browser sessions monitored in real time and file downloads blocked on these devices, while still allowing access.
questions.stem: Which Conditional Access control should Litware use?
options: Require Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device grant control
Conditional Access App Control session control with Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
questions.explain: Conditional Access App Control routes the session through Defender for Cloud Apps as a reverse proxy, allowing real-time monitoring and blocking downloads. Block access denies access entirely, hybrid join can't be met by personal laptops, and persistent browser session only controls staying signed in.

questions.stem: Before enforcing a new Conditional Access policy for all users, an administrator wants to see its impact in sign-in logs without affecting users. Which policy state should be used?
questions.explain: Report-only mode evaluates the policy and records the result in sign-in logs without enforcing it. On enforces the policy, Off doesn't evaluate it at all, and 'disabled for guests' isn't a policy state.

questions.stem: You are creating a Conditional Access policy with Microsoft Graph. The policy must require multifactor authentication for all users signing in to all apps. Complete the grant controls.
questions.explain: In the Graph conditionalAccessPolicy resource, builtInControls value mfa means Require multifactor authentication. compliantDevice requires an Intune-compliant device, block denies access, and passwordChange forces a password change (used for user risk policies).

questions.stem: You want a Conditional Access policy created through Microsoft Graph to be evaluated and logged but not enforced. Complete the property value.
questions.explain: The Graph state value enabledForReportingButNotEnforced is report-only mode: the policy is evaluated and results logged, but not enforced. enabled enforces it, disabled skips evaluation, and auditOnly isn't a valid value.

questions.stem: An auditor needs to view all settings in the Microsoft Entra admin center and Microsoft 365 admin center but must not be able to change anything. Which built-in role follows least privilege?
questions.explain: Global Reader is the read-only counterpart of Global Administrator and can view settings across admin centers without editing. Global Administrator and Security Administrator can make changes, and User Administrator manages users and groups.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Entra administrative roles, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Microsoft recommends having fewer than five Global Administrators.
You can edit the permissions included in a built-in Microsoft Entra role.
Microsoft recommends keeping cloud-only emergency access accounts for when normal administrators are locked out.

questions.explain: Best practice is fewer than five Global Administrators and two cloud-only emergency access accounts. Built-in role permissions are fixed; if none fit, create a custom role.

questions.stem: A helpdesk team must reset passwords for non-administrator users. Which role provides this with the least privilege?
questions.explain: Helpdesk Administrator can reset passwords for non-administrators and invalidate refresh tokens. Privileged Role Administrator manages role assignments, Global Administrator is far broader than needed, and Exchange Administrator manages Exchange Online.

questions.stem: Contoso wants its Paris helpdesk to manage only users in the Paris office, not users in other offices. What should be used to limit the scope of the helpdesk's role assignment?
questions.explain: Administrative units are containers that restrict a Microsoft Entra role's scope to a subset of users, groups or devices. Management groups scope Azure RBAC, dynamic groups manage membership not admin scope, and named locations are Conditional Access conditions.

questions.stem: A Microsoft Entra role assignment is made up of which THREE elements? Select THREE.
questions.explain: A role assignment attaches a role definition (the permissions) to a security principal (user, group or service principal) at a scope (tenant, administrative unit or resource). Conditional Access policies and authentication strengths control sign-in, not role assignments.

questions.case: A cloud engineer is assigned the Owner role on an Azure subscription. She tries to create new users in Microsoft Entra ID and gets an access denied error. Her manager is confused because 'Owner' sounds like full control.
questions.stem: What explains the error?
options: Owner is an Azure RBAC role for Azure resources and doesn't grant Microsoft Entra directory permissions
Owner permissions apply only after the engineer activates them in Conditional Access
Owner can create users only in an external tenant
The subscription must be added to an administrative unit first
questions.explain: Azure RBAC roles such as Owner, Contributor and Reader manage Azure resources through Azure Resource Manager; Microsoft Entra roles such as User Administrator manage directory objects. Conditional Access doesn't activate roles, and administrative units hold directory objects, not subscriptions.

questions.stem: No built-in Microsoft Entra role matches the exact app registration permissions a team needs. What should the administrator create?
options: An Azure custom role in the subscription
questions.explain: Custom Microsoft Entra roles are built from the same permission set used by built-in roles (and need P1 for assigned users). Azure custom roles can't contain Entra permissions. Conditional Access controls sign-in, and access packages bundle resource access, not admin permissions.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Entra solution helps ensure the right people have the right access to the right resources at the right time, and lets auditors verify the controls?
questions.explain: Microsoft Entra ID Governance covers identity and access lifecycle, access reviews, entitlement management and privileged access. Connect Sync is a hybrid sync tool, Verified ID issues verifiable credentials, and Defender for Identity detects attacks against on-premises AD DS.

questions.stem: HR wants new hires to automatically receive a welcome email and have their manager emailed a Temporary Access Pass before day one, and leavers to be removed from all groups on their last day. Which feature should you use?
questions.explain: Lifecycle workflows automate joiner, mover and leaver tasks triggered by dates such as hire or leave date, including TAP generation, welcome emails and group removal. Access reviews recertify existing access, PIM handles privileged roles, and administrative units scope admins.

questions.stem: Put the stages of the identity lifecycle in order for a typical employee.
options: Joiner: the account is created and initial access granted
Mover: access changes when the employee changes role or department
Leaver: access is removed and the account disabled
The disabled account is deleted after the retention period
questions.explain: Identity governance follows the joiner, mover, leaver lifecycle. Accounts are created at hire, access adjusts as people move, access is removed when they leave, and the disabled account is eventually deleted.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Entra ID Governance, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Lifecycle workflows require a Microsoft Entra ID Governance (or Microsoft Entra Suite) licence; Microsoft Entra ID P2 alone isn't enough.
Inbound provisioning can create user accounts from an HR system such as Workday.
Identity governance applies only to employees and can't manage guest users.

questions.explain: Lifecycle workflows are an ID Governance feature not included in P2. HR-driven inbound provisioning creates accounts from systems such as Workday or SuccessFactors. Governance also covers guests, for example through access reviews and entitlement management.

questions.stem: In entitlement management, what is a bundle of groups, applications and SharePoint Online sites that users can request as a single unit?
questions.explain: An access package bundles resource roles that users request together, with policies for approval and expiration. A catalog is the container holding resources and packages, administrative units scope admin roles, and a connected organization is a partner whose users can request access.

questions.case: Fabrikam is starting an eight-month project with Tailspin Toys. Tailspin engineers need a Teams team, a SharePoint site and a project app. Fabrikam wants Tailspin users to request access themselves, the project lead to approve each request, and guest accounts removed automatically when access expires.
questions.stem: Which solution meets the requirements with the least administrative effort?
options: Invite each engineer as a B2B guest and add them to the resources manually
Configure B2B direct connect with Tailspin
Run a quarterly access review of the Teams team
Create an access package in entitlement management with Tailspin as a connected organization
questions.explain: An access package with a connected organization lets Tailspin users request access, routes approval to the lead, sets expiry, and removes guests automatically when access ends. Manual invites need ongoing effort, direct connect covers Teams shared channels only, and access reviews don't handle requests.

questions.stem: Which TWO settings can be defined in an access package policy in entitlement management? Select TWO.
options: Who can request the access package
The minimum password length for requestors
Which Conditional Access session controls apply to SharePoint
questions.explain: Access package policies define who can request, approval requirements, expiration and reviews. Password length, Conditional Access session controls and method registration are configured elsewhere in Microsoft Entra ID.

questions.stem: Legal requires users to accept an acceptable-use document before accessing a payroll application. How is this enforced in Microsoft Entra?
options: Configure terms of use and require them with a Conditional Access grant control
Add the document to an access package catalog
Use a lifecycle workflow to email the document
Create a custom banned password list
questions.explain: Terms of use are uploaded in Microsoft Entra and enforced with the Conditional Access grant control Require terms of use. Catalogs hold resources, not acceptance documents, a lifecycle workflow email doesn't force acceptance, and banned password lists are unrelated.

questions.stem: Which feature lets group owners periodically confirm whether members and guests still need access to a Microsoft 365 group?
questions.explain: Access reviews let owners, managers or users recertify group memberships and app assignments on a schedule. PIM alerts flag privileged-role issues, lifecycle workflows automate joiner/mover/leaver tasks, and ID Protection detects risk.

questions.stem: Which THREE can be reviewed by using Microsoft Entra access reviews? Select THREE.
options: Members of security groups and Microsoft 365 groups
Users assigned to an enterprise application
Files stored in a user's OneDrive
Firewall rules on Azure virtual networks
questions.explain: Access reviews cover group memberships, application assignments, access packages and Microsoft Entra and Azure resource roles (through PIM). OneDrive file contents and network firewall rules aren't identity access assignments, so they can't be reviewed with access reviews.

questions.case: Contoso has 400 guests in a partner extranet group. Many projects ended long ago. Compliance requires that every quarter someone confirms whether each guest still needs access, that guests who aren't approved lose access without IT manually removing them, and that reviewers see which guests haven't signed in recently.
questions.stem: What should Contoso configure?
options: A Conditional Access policy that requires MFA for guests
A recurring quarterly access review with recommendations and auto apply results enabled
An entitlement management catalog for the extranet group
A PIM for Groups eligible assignment for each guest
questions.explain: A recurring access review can show inactivity-based recommendations and, with auto apply, removes denied guests automatically. MFA doesn't remove stale access, a catalog alone doesn't recertify existing members, and PIM for Groups gives just-in-time membership rather than periodic recertification.

questions.stem: An administrator runs an access review of an application's assigned users. Put the steps in order.
options: Create the review and choose the application, reviewers and recurrence
Reviewers receive a notification and the review starts
Reviewers approve or deny each user's continued access
The review ends and results are applied, removing denied users
questions.explain: An admin first defines the scope, reviewers and schedule. Reviewers are notified when the review starts and record decisions. When the review period ends, results are applied (automatically if auto apply is on), removing denied users.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Entra feature provides just-in-time, time-bound activation of administrator roles?
questions.explain: PIM makes users eligible for roles that they activate when needed for a limited time. Conditional Access controls sign-in conditions, entitlement management handles access package requests, and Entra Connect synchronizes on-premises identities.

questions.stem: For each statement about Privileged Identity Management, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A user with an eligible assignment must activate the role before using its permissions.
PIM can manage Azure resource roles as well as Microsoft Entra roles.
PIM is included with Microsoft Entra ID Free.

questions.explain: Eligible assignments must be activated, while active assignments are always in effect. PIM manages Microsoft Entra roles, Azure resource roles and group membership or ownership. It requires Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance.

questions.case: An audit found that eight engineers hold the Exchange Administrator role permanently, although each uses it a few hours a month. The CISO wants no standing access: engineers must activate the role only when needed, complete MFA, give a reason, get approval from the messaging lead, and lose the role automatically after four hours.
questions.stem: What should be implemented?
options: A Conditional Access policy requiring MFA for Exchange Online
A quarterly access review of the Exchange Administrator role
Eligible assignments in Privileged Identity Management with approval and a four-hour maximum activation
An access package that contains the Exchange Online app
questions.explain: PIM eligible assignments with role settings for MFA, justification, approval and maximum activation duration remove standing access. Conditional Access only adds sign-in conditions. Access reviews recertify roles periodically but leave standing access between reviews. Access packages grant resource access, not just-in-time admin roles.

questions.stem: Which TWO capabilities does Privileged Identity Management provide? Select TWO.
options: Notifications when privileged roles are activated
Downloadable audit history of role activations and assignments
Blocking weak passwords on domain controllers
Synchronizing administrator accounts from AD DS
Detecting leaked credentials on the dark web
questions.explain: PIM sends notifications on activation and keeps audit history that can be downloaded for auditors. Blocking weak passwords is Password Protection, synchronization is Entra Connect or Cloud Sync, and leaked credentials detection is ID Protection.

questions.stem: A user with an eligible PIM assignment needs to use the Security Administrator role. Put the steps in order.
options: The user opens Privileged Identity Management and selects the eligible role
The user completes MFA and enters a justification
An approver approves the activation request
The role becomes active for the configured duration
The role assignment expires automatically at the end of the duration
questions.explain: The user requests activation from PIM, satisfies MFA and justification requirements, waits for approval if required, and then holds the role for the limited activation time. When the time ends, the role returns to eligible automatically.

questions.stem: Microsoft finds a user's username and password pair in a public credential dump. Which risk does Microsoft Entra ID Protection raise?
options: Sign-in risk for an anonymous IP address
Device risk for a non-compliant device
questions.explain: Leaked credentials is a user risk detection because the account itself is likely compromised. Anonymous IP address and atypical travel are sign-in risk detections, and device compliance comes from Intune, not ID Protection.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Entra ID Protection, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Sign-in risk represents the probability that a given authentication request isn't from the identity owner.
A sign-in from a Tor exit node can trigger an anonymous IP address detection.
All risk detections are calculated only offline, after the sign-in finishes.

questions.explain: Sign-in risk measures whether a specific authentication is unauthorized, and Tor or anonymizer IPs trigger the anonymous IP address detection. Some detections are real-time during sign-in, while others are calculated offline afterwards.

questions.stem: A user signs in from Auckland and, 20 minutes later, from Paris. Which ID Protection detection is most likely?
questions.explain: Atypical travel flags two sign-ins from locations too far apart to travel between in the elapsed time. Leaked credentials comes from credential dumps, password spray from many accounts tried with common passwords, and admin confirmed compromised is a manual action.

questions.stem: Using risk-based Conditional Access, which control is typically required for a user with high user risk so the user can self-remediate?
options: Require device to be marked as compliant
questions.explain: User risk means the account may be compromised, so Microsoft recommends a secure password change (or risk remediation), which clears the risk. Device compliance, terms of use and app protection policies don't address compromised credentials.

questions.case: Adventure Works has Microsoft Entra ID P2. The security team wants users whose sign-in is rated medium or high risk to prove their identity with MFA rather than being blocked, so they can keep working. Some users haven't registered any MFA method yet.
questions.stem: Which configuration best meets the goal?
options: A user risk policy requiring password change, plus smart lockout
Security defaults, plus a custom banned password list
A PIM activation policy, plus an access review of all users
A sign-in risk Conditional Access policy requiring MFA for medium and high risk, plus the MFA registration policy
questions.explain: A sign-in risk policy requiring MFA lets genuine users self-remediate, and the MFA registration policy ensures users have a method registered so they aren't blocked. Password change targets user risk, security defaults can't use risk levels, and PIM and access reviews don't evaluate sign-in risk.

questions.stem: Which TWO reports can administrators use to investigate risk in Microsoft Entra ID Protection? Select TWO.
questions.explain: ID Protection provides the risky users, risky sign-ins and risk detections reports. Access package assignments belong to entitlement management, workflow history to lifecycle workflows, and sync errors to Microsoft Entra Connect Health.

questions.stem: You are creating a risk-based Conditional Access policy with Microsoft Graph. It must require MFA when sign-in risk is medium or high. Complete the condition.
questions.explain: signInRiskLevels is the condition for sign-in risk from ID Protection and pairs with an MFA requirement. userRiskLevels is for user risk (usually paired with password change), servicePrincipalRiskLevels targets workload identities, and insiderRiskLevels relates to Purview Insider Risk Management.

questions.stem: Which DDoS protection does every Azure resource with a public IP address receive at no additional cost?
options: Infrastructure-level DDoS protection that requires no configuration
Support from the DDoS Rapid Response team during an attack
Cost protection credits for resources that scale out during an attack
Attack mitigation reports and alerts in Azure Monitor
questions.explain: Azure applies infrastructure DDoS protection automatically and free to services with public IPs. Rapid Response and cost protection come only with DDoS Network Protection, and mitigation reports and alerts are features of the paid tiers, not the free baseline.

questions.stem: A company wants access to Microsoft's DDoS Rapid Response team and credits for scale-out costs caused by an attack. What should it enable?
options: Azure Web Application Firewall on Azure Front Door
questions.explain: DDoS Network Protection includes Rapid Response support, cost protection and a WAF discount. DDoS IP Protection provides core mitigation and telemetry but not those extras. Azure Firewall and WAF are separate services that offer neither benefit.

questions.stem: Which TWO attack categories does Azure DDoS Protection mitigate automatically at layers 3 and 4? Select TWO.
options: Volumetric attacks such as UDP floods
Protocol attacks such as SYN floods
SQL injection against a web form
Cross-site scripting in a web page
Password spray against Microsoft Entra ID
questions.explain: DDoS Protection handles network-layer volumetric and protocol attacks. SQL injection and XSS are layer 7 web attacks that need a WAF, and password spray is an identity attack addressed by Entra ID features such as Smart lockout and ID Protection.

questions.stem: For each statement about Azure DDoS Protection tiers, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: DDoS IP Protection is billed per protected public IP address.
DDoS IP Protection includes support from the DDoS Rapid Response team.
DDoS Network Protection is enabled by associating a DDoS protection plan with virtual networks.

questions.explain: IP Protection is a per-IP SKU covering core mitigation, metrics and alerts. Rapid Response, cost protection and the WAF discount are only in Network Protection, which is applied by linking a DDoS protection plan to VNets.

questions.case: Fabrikam hosts a public shopping site on VMs behind Azure Application Gateway. During a recent incident the site suffered a UDP flood against its public IP and, at the same time, thousands of HTTP requests containing SQL injection payloads. Fabrikam wants Microsoft-managed protection against both kinds of attack.
questions.stem: Which combination should Fabrikam use?
options: Azure DDoS Network Protection plus Azure WAF on Application Gateway
Azure DDoS IP Protection on its own
Network security groups plus Azure Bastion
Azure Firewall Basic plus Azure Key Vault
questions.explain: DDoS Protection mitigates the L3/L4 UDP flood, and Microsoft recommends a WAF for layer 7 attacks such as SQL injection. DDoS IP Protection alone doesn't inspect HTTP payloads. NSGs, Bastion, Firewall Basic and Key Vault don't block SQL injection in web requests.

questions.stem: Microsoft recommends combining Azure DDoS Protection with which service to defend against layer 7 attacks such as HTTP floods?
questions.explain: Layer 7 (application) attacks are handled by a WAF, such as WAF on Application Gateway or Front Door. Bastion secures RDP/SSH, NSGs filter L3/L4 traffic, and Entra ID Protection detects identity risk.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes Azure Firewall?
options: A host-based firewall agent you install and patch on each virtual machine
A free filter of allow and deny rules associated with subnets and network interfaces
A browser-based service that provides RDP and SSH access to VMs
A managed, cloud-native stateful firewall service with built-in high availability
questions.explain: Azure Firewall is a managed firewall-as-a-service with built-in HA and autoscaling. The free subnet/NIC filter describes an NSG, browser-based RDP/SSH is Azure Bastion, and Azure Firewall is not an agent installed on VMs.

questions.stem: You need Azure Firewall to allow VMs to make outbound HTTPS connections only to *.contoso-partner.com. Which rule type should you create?
questions.explain: Application rules filter outbound HTTP/HTTPS by FQDN and support wildcards such as *.contoso-partner.com. DNAT rules translate inbound traffic, network rules work on IPs, ports and protocols, and an NSG rule is a different service that can't filter by domain name.

questions.stem: Which Azure Firewall SKU adds TLS inspection and signature-based intrusion detection and prevention (IDPS)?
questions.explain: Premium adds TLS inspection, IDPS and full-path URL filtering for highly sensitive workloads. Standard offers threat intelligence and web categories, Basic is for small environments, and Firewall Manager is a central management tool, not a SKU.

questions.stem: Which TWO capabilities are included in Azure Firewall Standard? Select TWO.
options: Threat intelligence-based filtering that can alert on and deny known malicious IPs and domains
Filtering outbound web traffic by web categories
TLS inspection of outbound encrypted traffic
questions.explain: Standard supports threat intelligence filtering in alert-and-deny mode and web categories. TLS inspection and IDPS are Premium-only features, so a Standard firewall can't provide them.

questions.stem: For each statement about Azure Firewall, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Azure Firewall in a hub virtual network can filter traffic between spoke virtual networks.
You must deploy and patch extra virtual machines to scale Azure Firewall.
A DNAT rule can translate inbound traffic on the firewall's public IP to a private IP address.

questions.explain: With user-defined routes, spoke-to-spoke traffic passes through the hub firewall. Azure Firewall is a managed service with built-in HA and autoscaling, so there are no VMs to manage. DNAT rules publish internal services through the firewall's public IP.

questions.case: Northwind has 12 virtual networks in Azure. The security team must allow outbound internet access only to an approved list of domain names, apply the same rules to every VNet, and keep central logs of allowed and denied connections for Microsoft Sentinel.
questions.stem: What should Northwind implement?
options: A network security group on every subnet with Internet service tag rules
Azure Firewall in a hub virtual network, with user-defined routes from each spoke
Azure DDoS Network Protection linked to all 12 virtual networks
Azure Bastion Standard deployed in each virtual network
questions.explain: A hub Azure Firewall gives one central policy with FQDN-based application rules and central logging, and UDRs send spoke traffic through it. NSGs can't filter by domain name and are managed per subnet. DDoS Protection and Bastion don't control outbound access.

questions.stem: What is Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) mainly designed to protect against?
options: Brute-force RDP attempts against virtual machine management ports
Volumetric UDP floods against public IP addresses
Common web exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting
Secrets accidentally committed to application source code
questions.explain: WAF inspects HTTP/HTTPS requests and blocks common exploits like SQL injection and XSS. RDP brute force is addressed by Bastion or JIT, UDP floods by DDoS Protection, and secrets in code by Defender for Cloud DevOps security.

questions.stem: On which TWO Azure services can you deploy Azure Web Application Firewall? Select TWO.
questions.explain: Azure WAF runs on Application Gateway (regional), Front Door (global edge), Application Gateway for Containers and Azure CDN. Bastion, VPN Gateway and Key Vault don't host WAF policies.

questions.stem: A WAF policy is set to Detection mode. What happens when a request matches a managed rule?
options: The request is blocked and the client receives a 403 response
Managed rules are skipped and only custom rules are evaluated
The request is held until an administrator approves it
The match is logged and the request is allowed through
questions.explain: Detection mode monitors and logs threats without blocking. Prevention mode is the one that blocks and returns 403. WAF has no approval queue, and Detection mode still evaluates managed rules.

questions.stem: You are introducing Azure WAF in front of a production web app and want to avoid blocking legitimate users. Put the steps in order.
options: Associate a WAF policy in Detection mode
Review WAF logs for false positives
Add exclusions or custom rules to tune the policy
Switch the policy to Prevention mode
questions.explain: Microsoft recommends running a new WAF in Detection mode first, reviewing the logs, tuning exclusions and custom rules, and only then switching to Prevention mode so real attacks are blocked without breaking valid traffic.

questions.stem: A company serves its web app through Azure Front Door and must block all requests from two specific countries. What should it configure?
options: A WAF custom rule with a geo-match condition
A network security group rule using the Internet service tag
Azure DDoS IP Protection on the origin
A Conditional Access policy with named locations
questions.explain: WAF custom rules can match on the client's country (geo-filtering) and block it at the Front Door edge. NSG service tags don't represent countries, DDoS Protection doesn't filter by geography, and Conditional Access controls Entra ID sign-ins, not anonymous web traffic.

questions.stem: For each statement about Azure WAF, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: WAF on Azure Front Door can block malicious requests at Microsoft's network edge before they reach the origin.
Azure WAF managed rules are based on Microsoft's Default Rule Set or the OWASP Core Rule Set.
Deploying WAF removes the need for protection against volumetric network-layer floods.

questions.explain: Front Door WAF filters at the global edge, and managed rules come from DRS or OWASP CRS. WAF inspects layer 7 requests; volumetric L3/L4 floods still need Azure DDoS Protection, so the services complement each other.

questions.stem: VMs in two separate Azure virtual networks must communicate using private IP addresses over the Microsoft backbone. What should you configure?
questions.explain: VNets are isolated by default; peering connects them privately over Microsoft's backbone. NSGs and ASGs filter traffic but don't create connectivity, and Bastion provides admin RDP/SSH, not VNet-to-VNet routing.

questions.stem: For each statement about Azure virtual networks, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: By default, resources in different subnets of the same virtual network can communicate.
A single virtual network can span multiple Azure regions.
If VNet A is peered with VNet B and VNet B is peered with VNet C, VNet A can reach VNet C automatically.

questions.explain: Subnets within a VNet route to each other by default, so you add NSGs to restrict them. A VNet is scoped to one region. Peering is non-transitive, so A and C need their own peering or routing through a hub.

questions.stem: In a hub-and-spoke design, you must force all internet-bound traffic from a spoke subnet through Azure Firewall in the hub. What should you associate with the spoke subnet?
options: A route table with a user-defined route
questions.explain: A user-defined route in a route table overrides default routing and sends traffic to the firewall's private IP as the next hop. An NSG only allows or denies traffic, a service tag is an IP group used in rules, and a private DNS zone resolves names.

questions.case: Tailspin runs a three-tier app (web, application, database) in Azure. Following Zero Trust, the CISO wants a compromised web server to be unable to connect directly to the database. Only the application tier may reach the database on its SQL port.
questions.stem: Which design meets the requirement?
options: Place all three tiers in one subnet and monitor them with Defender for Cloud secure score
Give each tier a public IP address and protect it with DDoS IP Protection
Store each tier's IP addresses as secrets in Azure Key Vault
Put each tier in its own subnet and use NSGs to allow only the required flows between them
questions.explain: Separate subnets plus NSG rules segment the tiers, so the database subnet accepts SQL traffic only from the application subnet, limiting lateral movement. Secure score only measures posture, public IPs increase exposure, and Key Vault doesn't control network flows.

questions.stem: An app in a virtual network must reach an Azure SQL database through a private IP address in that VNet, without traffic going to the database's public endpoint. What should you use?
options: A service tag in an NSG rule
questions.explain: A private endpoint gives the PaaS resource a private IP inside your VNet, so traffic stays on the private network. Service tags only name IP ranges in rules, Bastion is for admin RDP/SSH, and DDoS IP Protection defends public IPs.

questions.stem: To which resources can you associate a network security group (NSG)?
options: Microsoft Entra ID users and groups
questions.explain: An NSG is associated with a subnet, a VM's network interface, or both. Management groups and subscriptions are scopes for Azure Policy and RBAC, Entra users and groups are identities, and key vaults and storage accounts use their own firewalls or private endpoints.

questions.stem: An NSG has two inbound rules: priority 100 denies TCP 3389 from Any, and priority 200 allows TCP 3389 from the Internet service tag. What happens to an RDP connection from the internet?
options: It is allowed, because Allow rules always take precedence over Deny rules
It is denied, because rule 100 is processed first and processing stops at the first match
It is allowed, because rule 200 names a more specific source
It is denied only by the default DenyAllInbound rule at priority 65500
questions.explain: NSG rules are evaluated from the lowest priority number up, and the first match decides. Rule 100 matches and denies the traffic, so rule 200 is never reached. NSGs don't prefer Allow rules or more specific sources, and the default rule isn't involved.

questions.stem: For each statement about network security groups, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: If an outbound rule allows a connection, the response traffic is allowed back automatically.
You can delete the default DenyAllInbound rule from an NSG.
Custom security rules use priority values from 100 to 4096.

questions.explain: NSGs are stateful, so return traffic for an allowed flow is permitted. Default rules can't be deleted, only overridden by higher-priority custom rules. Custom rule priorities range from 100 to 4096.

questions.stem: Complete the Azure CLI command so the rule permits inbound HTTPS traffic to the subnet protected by nsg-web.
questions.code: az network nsg rule create --resource-group rg-web --nsg-name nsg-web --name AllowHTTPS --priority 110 --direction Inbound --access ____ --protocol Tcp --destination-port-ranges 443
questions.explain: An NSG rule's action (access) is either Allow or Deny, so --access Allow permits the traffic. Permit, Accept and Enable aren't valid values for an NSG rule action.

questions.stem: A VM has an NSG on its subnet and another NSG on its network interface. Put the steps that inbound internet traffic follows in order.
options: Traffic arrives at the virtual network
Rules in the subnet's NSG are evaluated
Rules in the network interface's NSG are evaluated
Traffic is delivered to the VM
questions.explain: For inbound traffic Azure evaluates the subnet NSG first, then the NIC NSG, and the traffic must be allowed by both before it reaches the VM. Outbound traffic is evaluated in the reverse order: NIC NSG first, then subnet NSG.

questions.stem: Which TWO can you use as the source or destination of an NSG security rule instead of listing IP addresses? Select TWO.
questions.explain: Service tags (such as Internet or Storage) and application security groups can replace explicit IPs in NSG rules. Entra security groups and named locations are identity constructs for access policies, and Key Vault references aren't valid in NSG rules.

questions.stem: Which default NSG rule blocks inbound traffic that no higher-priority rule has allowed?
questions.explain: DenyAllInbound (priority 65500) is the final inbound catch-all deny. AllowVNetInBound and AllowAzureLoadBalancerInBound allow specific inbound traffic, and AllowInternetOutBound is an outbound rule.

questions.stem: Which Azure service lets administrators connect to VMs over RDP or SSH from the Azure portal over TLS, without the VMs having public IP addresses?
questions.explain: Azure Bastion brokers RDP/SSH from the browser over TLS to the VM's private IP. JIT only opens management ports temporarily, VPN Gateway needs client or site VPN setup, and Azure Firewall filters traffic rather than providing remote sessions.

questions.stem: An administrator connects to a VM through Azure Bastion from a web browser. Put the steps in order.
options: Sign in to the Azure portal
Select the VM and choose Connect, then Bastion
The browser opens a TLS session on port 443 to Azure Bastion
Azure Bastion opens an RDP or SSH session to the VM's private IP address
questions.explain: The admin signs in to the portal, picks the VM and chooses Bastion. The browser talks to Bastion over TLS on 443, and Bastion then connects to the VM's private IP inside the VNet, so RDP/SSH is never exposed to the internet.

questions.stem: Where must Azure Bastion (Basic, Standard or Premium SKU) be deployed?
options: On each virtual machine as a VM extension
In a dedicated subnet named AzureBastionSubnet in the virtual network
In the GatewaySubnet alongside the VPN gateway
In any subnet that already contains virtual machines
questions.explain: Bastion needs its own subnet named AzureBastionSubnet, sized /26 or larger. It isn't a VM extension, GatewaySubnet is reserved for VPN/ExpressRoute gateways, and it can't share a subnet with workload VMs.

questions.case: Litware's auditors require that every administrative RDP and SSH session to production VMs is recorded for later review. Litware also wants the Bastion deployment itself to have no public IP address.
questions.stem: Which Azure Bastion SKU should Litware choose?
questions.explain: Session recording and private-only deployment are Premium features. Standard adds native client support, shareable links and IP-based connection but not recording. Basic offers browser RDP/SSH only, and Developer is a free shared SKU not meant for production.

questions.stem: An engineer wants to use their local SSH client, through the Azure CLI, to connect to a VM via Azure Bastion Standard. Complete the command.
questions.code: az network bastion ____ --name bas-hub --resource-group rg-hub --target-resource-id $vmId --auth-type ssh-key --username azureuser --ssh-key ~/.ssh/id_rsa
questions.explain: az network bastion ssh opens an SSH session through Bastion with the native client, which requires Standard or Premium. The rdp subcommand is for Windows RDP via mstsc, tunnel creates a port tunnel and doesn't take SSH auth options, and connect isn't a valid subcommand.

questions.stem: Which THREE object types can Azure Key Vault store and manage? Select THREE.
questions.explain: Key Vault manages secrets (passwords, connection strings), keys (encryption and signing) and certificates. NSG rules belong to network security groups, and Conditional Access policies are configured in Microsoft Entra ID.

questions.stem: A web app must read a database connection string from Azure Key Vault without any credential stored in its configuration. What should the app use to authenticate to Key Vault?
options: A managed identity in Microsoft Entra ID
A local account stored in the app's settings
questions.explain: Key Vault authenticates callers through Microsoft Entra ID, and a managed identity gives the app an Entra identity with no secret to store. SAS tokens and account keys are storage credentials, and a local account would put a credential back in configuration.

questions.stem: For each statement about Azure Key Vault, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Soft-delete is enabled by default on new key vaults and cannot be disabled once enabled.
Purge protection is enabled by default on every new key vault.
The Premium tier supports keys protected by hardware security modules (HSMs).

questions.explain: Soft-delete is on by default and can't be turned off, with 7-90 days retention. Purge protection is optional and off by default. Premium adds HSM-protected keys; Standard uses software-protected keys.

questions.stem: You must grant an application permission to read secret values in a key vault that uses the Azure RBAC permission model, following least privilege. Which built-in role should you assign?
questions.explain: Key Vault Secrets User can read secret contents and nothing more. Key Vault Reader sees metadata but not secret values. Secrets Officer can also create and delete secrets, and Administrator has full data-plane control, both more than needed.

questions.stem: Complete the Azure CLI command so deleted vaults and objects cannot be permanently purged until the retention period ends.
questions.code: az keyvault create --name kv-contoso-prod --resource-group rg-sec --location westeurope --retention-days 90 ____ true
questions.explain: --enable-purge-protection true stops anyone purging deleted items before retention ends. Soft-delete is already on by default and only makes items recoverable, RBAC authorization sets the permission model, and disk-encryption access lets Azure Disk Encryption fetch secrets.

questions.stem: Microsoft Defender for Cloud is best described as which type of solution?
options: A security information and event management (SIEM) solution
questions.explain: Defender for Cloud is a CNAPP that combines DevSecOps, CSPM and CWPP. Microsoft Sentinel is the SIEM, Defender for Cloud Apps is the CASB, and Microsoft Entra ID is the identity provider.

questions.stem: Which THREE capability areas does Microsoft Defender for Cloud combine? Select THREE.
questions.explain: Defender for Cloud's CNAPP pillars are DevSecOps, CSPM and CWPP. Mobile device management is handled by Microsoft Intune, and access reviews are part of Microsoft Entra ID Governance.

questions.stem: A SOC wants Defender for Cloud security alerts correlated with logs from firewalls, Microsoft 365 and on-premises servers so analysts can hunt across all of them. Where should the alerts be sent?
questions.explain: Defender for Cloud alerts can be exported to a SIEM/SOAR such as Microsoft Sentinel, which correlates many data sources and supports hunting. Key Vault stores secrets, Compliance Manager tracks regulatory compliance, and Firewall Manager manages firewall policies.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Defender for Cloud coverage, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Defender for Cloud can assess AWS accounts and GCP projects after you add a connector.
Defender for Cloud can protect only resources hosted in Azure.
Defender for Cloud can connect to GitHub repositories to find issues such as infrastructure-as-code misconfigurations.

questions.explain: Connectors bring AWS and GCP into the same posture view, on-premises machines are covered through Azure Arc or Defender for Endpoint, so it isn't Azure-only. DevOps security connects Azure DevOps, GitHub and GitLab to surface IaC and secret findings.

questions.stem: Microsoft recommends onboarding on-premises Windows and Linux servers in which way so they receive the full set of Defender for Servers features?
options: As members of an application security group
questions.explain: Azure Arc projects non-Azure servers into Azure Resource Manager, so Defender for Cloud plans and recommendations apply fully. Entra join is a device identity state, ASGs group NICs for NSG rules, and an AWS connector is for AWS accounts.

questions.stem: Which TWO capabilities are included in free Foundational CSPM in Microsoft Defender for Cloud? Select TWO.
options: Security recommendations based on the Microsoft cloud security benchmark
Risk hunting with cloud security explorer
questions.explain: Foundational CSPM includes secure score and MCSB-based recommendations at no cost. Attack path analysis, agentless VM scanning and cloud security explorer all require the paid Defender CSPM plan.

questions.case: Adatum has hundreds of recommendations in Defender for Cloud. The security lead wants to see which weaknesses an attacker could chain together, for example an internet-exposed VM with a known vulnerability that has permissions to a storage account holding sensitive data, so the team can fix those first.
questions.stem: Which capability should Adatum use, and which plan does it need?
options: Regulatory compliance dashboard, in Foundational CSPM
Attack path analysis, in Defender CSPM
File integrity monitoring, in Defender for Servers Plan 1
questions.explain: Attack path analysis maps exploitable chains toward critical assets and requires Defender CSPM. Secure score measures posture without showing paths, regulatory compliance also needs a paid plan, and FIM is a Plan 2 server feature that detects file changes.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of cloud security posture management (CSPM)?
options: Detecting malware running on virtual machines in real time
Continuously identifying misconfigurations and weaknesses and guiding you to fix them
Collecting and correlating security logs from every source for threat hunting
Encrypting data stored in cloud storage accounts
questions.explain: CSPM assesses configurations and gives hardening guidance to prevent breaches. Real-time malware detection is workload protection (CWPP), log correlation and hunting is a SIEM function, and encryption is handled by storage and Key Vault features.

questions.stem: For each statement about Defender CSPM, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Defender CSPM can scan VMs for vulnerabilities and secrets without installing an agent.
Defender CSPM includes governance rules to assign owners and due dates for remediation at scale.
Defender CSPM is required to see a secure score.

questions.explain: Agentless VM vulnerability and secrets scanning and governance rules are Defender CSPM features. Secure score is already part of free Foundational CSPM, so the paid plan isn't needed for it.

questions.stem: Which security standard does Microsoft Defender for Cloud apply by default when you enable it on an Azure subscription?
questions.explain: MCSB is the default standard and the basis of recommendations and secure score. PCI DSS, ISO 27001 and NIST SP 800-53 are regulatory standards you can add after enabling a qualifying paid Defender plan.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to show how Defender for Cloud turns a security standard into action.
options: A security standard such as MCSB is assigned to the subscription
Defender for Cloud continuously assesses resources against the standard's controls
A resource that fails a control is marked unhealthy
A security recommendation with remediation steps is generated
The resource owner remediates the issue and the resource becomes healthy
questions.explain: Standards define controls, resources are assessed against them, failures mark resources unhealthy, Defender for Cloud generates recommendations with remediation steps, and fixing them returns the resource to healthy and improves secure score.

questions.stem: An administrator wants to stop anyone from creating new storage accounts that violate a Defender for Cloud recommendation, rather than fixing them after deployment. Which option should they use on the recommendation?
questions.explain: Deny (like Enforce) uses Azure Policy to stop noncompliant resources being created. Exempt excludes a resource from the recommendation, Fix remediates resources that already exist, and assigning an owner is governance that tracks remediation without blocking deployments.

questions.case: Woodgrove Bank must show auditors how its Azure and AWS environments measure against PCI DSS. Only the free Foundational CSPM is enabled today. The security team opens the regulatory compliance dashboard but cannot add PCI DSS.
questions.stem: What must Woodgrove do first?
options: Assign the Security Reader role to the auditors
Enable at least one paid Defender for Cloud plan, such as Defender CSPM
Raise the subscription's secure score above 80 percent
Create a Key Vault to store the PCI DSS assessment results
questions.explain: Adding regulatory standards such as PCI DSS requires a paid Defender for Cloud plan (any except Servers Plan 1 or APIs Plan 1); Defender CSPM qualifies. Role assignments, secure score values and Key Vault don't unlock compliance standards.

questions.stem: Complete the Azure Resource Graph query to list Defender for Cloud recommendation assessments.
questions.code:
securityresources
| where type == "microsoft.security/____"
| project id, name, properties.displayName, properties.status.code
questions.explain: Recommendations are stored as microsoft.security/assessments resources, each with a display name and a status code such as Healthy or Unhealthy. Alerts are threat detections, pricings hold plan settings, and securescores holds the score values rather than individual recommendations.

questions.stem: In Microsoft Defender for Cloud, what does a higher secure score indicate?
options: More security alerts were raised in the last 24 hours
More Defender plans are enabled on the subscription
A lower level of identified security risk
More resources are covered by Azure DDoS Protection
questions.explain: Secure score summarizes posture: a higher score means fewer identified risks. It isn't a count of alerts, enabled plans or DDoS-protected resources, and the 'Enable enhanced security features' control is worth no points.

questions.case: Contoso's 'Secure management ports' control has three recommendations across 20 VMs. The team fixes two of the recommendations on all 20 VMs, but the third recommendation remains unhealthy on five VMs.
questions.stem: What is true about Contoso's classic secure score for this control?
options: Contoso receives the control's full maximum points
Contoso does not yet receive the control's full maximum points
The control is removed from the score until all VMs are healthy
The score drops to zero for the whole subscription
questions.explain: A control's full points are earned only when all of its recommendations are remediated for all resources, so Contoso still has a potential score increase on this control. Unfinished controls aren't removed from the calculation, and the subscription's overall score doesn't drop to zero.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about secure score in Defender for Cloud are true? Select TWO.
options: Recommendations in preview do not affect the secure score
The secure score can be queried with Azure Resource Graph
Risk prioritization of recommendations changes the classic secure score
Only recommendations from regulatory compliance standards affect the score
questions.explain: Preview recommendations don't count until generally available, and scores can be queried with Azure Resource Graph or the REST API. Risk prioritization doesn't affect the classic score, and the score is based on built-in MCSB recommendations, not regulatory standards.

questions.stem: Which Defender for Cloud plan can scan files uploaded to a blob container for malware?
questions.explain: Defender for Storage provides malware scanning of uploads and detects suspicious storage access. Defender for Key Vault watches vault access, Defender for Resource Manager watches management operations, and Defender for App Service protects web apps.

questions.stem: A company has only free Foundational CSPM enabled. It now wants to receive security alerts when a VM shows signs of active compromise. What should it do?
options: Enable a cloud workload protection plan such as Defender for Servers
Add the ISO 27001 standard to the regulatory compliance dashboard
Deploy Azure Bastion in the VM's virtual network
Remediate every recommendation to reach a 100 percent secure score
questions.explain: Threat-detection alerts come from paid workload protection plans. Compliance standards and secure score are posture features that don't detect active attacks, and Bastion secures admin access but doesn't raise threat alerts.

questions.stem: Complete the Azure CLI command to enable Defender for Servers Plan 2 on the current subscription.
questions.code: az security pricing create --name VirtualMachines --tier ____ --subplan P2
questions.explain: Defender plans are enabled by setting a pricing tier of standard (paid); free turns the plan off. premium and enhanced aren't valid --tier values, even though the paid plans are described as enhanced security features.

questions.stem: For each statement about Defender for Cloud workload protection plans, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Defender for Resource Manager detects suspicious management operations against Azure resources.
Defender for Containers protects Kubernetes clusters, including runtime threat detection.
Defender for Key Vault stores secrets on behalf of applications.

questions.explain: Defender for Resource Manager watches the management layer, and Defender for Containers covers Kubernetes hardening, image vulnerabilities and runtime threats. Defender for Key Vault detects unusual access to vaults; storing secrets is the job of Azure Key Vault itself.

questions.stem: Which TWO features are included in Defender for Servers Plan 2 but NOT in Plan 1? Select TWO.
options: Integration with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
questions.explain: JIT VM access and file integrity monitoring are Plan 2 additions, along with agentless scanning and premium vulnerability management. Defender for Endpoint integration, which provides EDR, is already included in Plan 1.

questions.case: Proseware's VMs must keep RDP closed by default. Administrators occasionally need RDP access for a few hours, only from their own IP address, and the port must close automatically afterwards. Each request must be checked against the admin's Azure RBAC permissions on the VM.
questions.stem: Which feature meets these requirements?
options: A WAF custom rule on Application Gateway
Just-in-time VM access in Defender for Servers Plan 2
questions.explain: JIT keeps management ports locked with NSG deny rules, checks RBAC on request, opens the port only for the requester's IP and approved time, then restores the rules. DDoS Protection, WAF and threat intelligence filtering don't grant time-bound port access.

questions.stem: Which description best matches a security information and event management (SIEM) system?
options: It collects and correlates log data from many sources to detect threats and raise alerts
It runs automated playbooks that orchestrate response actions across security tools
It assesses cloud resources against a benchmark and produces a secure score
It stores cryptographic keys and secrets in hardware-backed vaults
questions.explain: A SIEM centralises, normalises and correlates security data to detect threats. Automated playbooks are SOAR. Benchmark-based scoring is cloud security posture management (Defender for Cloud). Key and secret storage is Azure Key Vault.

questions.stem: A SOC wants every high-severity incident to automatically block the attacker's IP on the firewall and open a ServiceNow ticket, without an analyst clicking anything. Which concept describes this?
questions.explain: Security orchestration, automation and response (SOAR) automates and coordinates response actions across tools with playbooks. SIEM detects and correlates but does not itself orchestrate responses. CSPM is posture management. A CASB controls cloud app usage.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Microsoft Sentinel provides both SIEM and SOAR capabilities.
The main purpose of a SIEM is to automatically patch vulnerable endpoints.
SOAR solutions use playbooks to orchestrate response actions across multiple tools.

questions.explain: Sentinel is Microsoft's cloud-native SIEM and SOAR. A SIEM collects and correlates data for detection; patching is vulnerability management. SOAR uses playbooks to automate and orchestrate response across tools.

questions.stem: Put the steps of a typical SIEM and SOAR workflow in order.
options: Collect log and event data from many sources
Normalize and correlate the data with detection rules
Raise alerts and group them into incidents
questions.explain: Data must be collected before it can be normalised and correlated. Correlation produces alerts that are grouped into incidents (SIEM), and incidents then trigger automated playbooks (SOAR).

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Sentinel feature is used to ingest data from sources such as Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft 365 and third-party firewalls?
questions.explain: Data connectors bring data into Sentinel, including Microsoft services and third-party sources via Syslog, CEF or APIs. Workbooks visualise data, analytics rules detect threats in data already ingested, and watchlists hold your own reference lists.

questions.stem: Which TWO are types of analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel? Select TWO.
questions.explain: Sentinel analytics rule types include scheduled query rules and near-real-time (NRT) rules, plus anomaly and threat intelligence rules. Access reviews belong to Entra ID Governance, retention labels to Microsoft Purview, and session policies to Defender for Cloud Apps.

questions.stem: You want a Sentinel query that counts failed Windows logons (event ID 4625) per account and shows accounts with more than 10 failures. Complete the query.
questions.code:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4625
| ____ FailedLogons = count() by Account
| where FailedLogons > 10
questions.explain: summarize aggregates rows, here with count() grouped by Account. project only selects columns, extend adds calculated columns without aggregating, and join combines two tables.

questions.stem: A SOC manager wants an interactive dashboard in Microsoft Sentinel that shows sign-in failures by country and trends over the last 30 days. What should be used?
questions.explain: Workbooks are interactive visual reports for monitoring Sentinel data and come with many templates. Notebooks are Jupyter-based code investigations, playbooks are Logic Apps automation, and watchlists are reference lists for correlation.

questions.stem: Microsoft Sentinel playbooks are built on which Azure service?
questions.explain: Sentinel playbooks are Azure Logic Apps workflows with a large connector gallery. Azure Functions and Automation runbooks are other automation services but not the basis of playbooks. Azure Monitor workbooks underpin Sentinel workbooks (visualisation).

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Sentinel, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Automation rules can run a playbook when an incident is created.
Threat hunting in Sentinel can only begin after an analytics rule has raised an alert.
Microsoft Sentinel can be used from the Microsoft Defender portal.

questions.explain: Automation rules triage incidents and can trigger playbooks. Hunting is proactive and does not need an alert. Sentinel is generally available in the Defender portal, and Microsoft plans to end Azure portal support after 31 March 2027.

questions.stem: While hunting, you want only failed Microsoft Entra sign-ins from the last day, counted per user and IP. Complete the query.
questions.code:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| ____ ResultType != "0"
| summarize Failures = count() by UserPrincipalName, IPAddress
questions.explain: where filters rows; ResultType "0" means success, so != "0" keeps failures. summarize aggregates, project selects columns and sort by orders results; none of them filter on a condition.

questions.stem: A team is deploying Microsoft Sentinel. Put the steps in order.
options: Connect data sources with data connectors
Respond with automation rules and playbooks
questions.explain: Sentinel follows collect, detect, investigate, respond: data is ingested by connectors, analytics rules raise incidents, analysts investigate them, and automation rules and playbooks carry out the response.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes Microsoft Defender XDR?
options: A cloud-native SIEM that ingests logs from any source through data connectors
A posture management tool that scores Azure resources against the Microsoft cloud security benchmark
A unified suite that correlates detection and response across endpoints, identities, email and cloud apps
A data governance service that classifies and labels sensitive information
questions.explain: Defender XDR is a unified pre- and post-breach suite coordinating protection across Microsoft workloads. The SIEM description is Microsoft Sentinel, benchmark scoring is Defender for Cloud, and classification and labelling is Microsoft Purview.

questions.stem: Which THREE services are part of Microsoft Defender XDR? Select THREE.
questions.explain: Defender XDR includes Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Office 365, Defender for Identity, Defender for Cloud Apps and Defender Vulnerability Management. Azure Key Vault is an Azure infrastructure service and Compliance Manager is part of Microsoft Purview.

questions.stem: An organization already uses Microsoft Defender XDR. It now needs to analyse logs from a third-party firewall and AWS CloudTrail alongside its Microsoft signals, with custom detection rules and long-term retention. What should it add?
questions.explain: Microsoft Sentinel is a SIEM that ingests data from almost any source, including third-party firewalls and other clouds, and complements Defender XDR. The other options protect specific Microsoft workloads and don't act as a general log platform.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Defender XDR, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Defender XDR can correlate alerts from several Defender services into a single incident.
Analysts must open a separate console for each Defender service to investigate one incident.
Alerts from Microsoft Entra ID Protection can appear in Defender XDR incidents.

questions.explain: Defender XDR correlates cross-domain alerts into one incident in the Microsoft Defender portal, so no separate consoles are needed. Microsoft Entra ID Protection alerts are integrated into Defender XDR incidents.

questions.case: At Fabrikam, a user receives a phishing email and opens the attachment. Malware runs on the user's laptop, and the attacker then uses the stolen credentials to query the on-premises domain controller for admin group members. Defender for Office 365, Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Identity each raise an alert.
questions.stem: What is the main benefit Microsoft Defender XDR provides in this scenario?
options: It forwards each alert separately to the owner of each product for review
It converts the alerts into Compliance Manager improvement actions
It disables all three services until a Global Administrator approves
It correlates the email, endpoint and identity alerts into one incident that shows the full attack story
questions.explain: Defender XDR's value is cross-domain correlation: the three alerts become one incident with the full attack chain, and response can happen across products. It doesn't silo alerts, Compliance Manager is a Purview compliance tool, and services aren't disabled.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Defender XDR capability automatically contains compromised users and devices during a high-confidence, in-progress attack such as human-operated ransomware?
questions.explain: Automatic attack disruption contains attacker-controlled assets, for example by containing a device or disabling a user. Threat analytics provides reports, Secure Score measures posture, and Cloud Discovery finds shadow IT.

questions.stem: In advanced hunting, you want PowerShell processes launched with an encoded command in the last 7 days. Complete the query.
questions.code:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "powershell.exe" and ProcessCommandLine ____ "-EncodedCommand"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
questions.explain: has is a string operator that tests whether a column contains a term, so it fits inside the where condition. summarize, project and extend are tabular operators that must follow a pipe, not string comparison operators.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Advanced hunting in Microsoft Defender XDR uses Kusto Query Language (KQL).
Actions taken by automatic attack disruption cannot be reversed by the security team.
A Defender XDR incident can include alerts from both Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Office 365.

questions.explain: Advanced hunting is KQL-based. All automatic attack disruption actions can be undone by the SOC, which stays in control. Incidents are cross-product, combining alerts from multiple Defender services.

questions.stem: Which TWO actions can automatic attack disruption in Microsoft Defender XDR take? Select TWO.
options: Permanently delete the user's OneDrive content
questions.explain: Attack disruption uses containment actions such as contain device (Defender for Endpoint) and disable user (Defender for Identity/Entra ID). It is designed to be reversible, so it does not reimage devices or delete data.

questions.stem: An analyst wants to approve remediation actions that automated investigation has recommended, and see actions already completed. Where in the Microsoft Defender portal should they go?
questions.explain: The Action center lists pending and completed remediation actions from automated and manual investigations. Threat analytics provides threat reports, Secure Score measures posture, and Exposure management covers attack surface and vulnerabilities.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Defender for Office 365 feature checks whether a URL is malicious at the moment a user clicks it?
questions.explain: Safe Links rewrites and verifies URLs at time of click. Safe Attachments sandboxes files, ZAP removes malicious messages after delivery, and attack simulation training runs phishing simulations for user education.

questions.stem: You want unknown email attachments opened in a virtual environment to observe their behaviour before the message is delivered. Which feature should you configure?
questions.explain: Safe Attachments detonates attachments in a sandbox before delivery to catch zero-day malware. Safe Links handles URLs, anti-spam policies filter junk mail, and spoof intelligence detects spoofed senders.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Exchange Online Protection (EOP) is included with all Microsoft 365 cloud mailboxes.
Safe Links and Safe Attachments are not included in Defender for Office 365 Plan 1.
Safe Attachments can protect files in SharePoint, OneDrive and Microsoft Teams.

questions.explain: EOP is the built-in baseline for every cloud mailbox. Safe Links and Safe Attachments are Plan 1 features (so also in Plan 2). Safe Attachments for SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams extends sandbox scanning to shared files.

questions.stem: In advanced hunting, you want the 10 senders of the most phishing emails in the last day. Complete the query.
questions.code:
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
