| where ThreatTypes has "Phish"
| ____ count() by SenderFromAddress
| top 10 by count_
questions.explain: summarize count() by SenderFromAddress aggregates messages per sender and creates the default count_ column used by top. project and extend don't aggregate, and order by sorts without grouping, so count_ would not exist.

questions.case: Finance staff at Contoso receive emails that appear to come from the CEO, sent from contoso-corp.com instead of contoso.com, asking for urgent wire transfers. The messages contain no links or attachments. Contoso has Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1.
questions.stem: Which capability should Contoso configure to best detect these messages?
options: Anti-phishing policy with user and domain impersonation protection
Connection filtering with an IP Allow List
Safe Attachments policy in Dynamic Delivery mode
questions.explain: Impersonation protection in Defender for Office 365 anti-phishing policies detects messages pretending to be specific users (the CEO) or lookalike domains. Outbound spam covers mail leaving the tenant, an IP Allow List would weaken filtering, and Safe Attachments needs attachments.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Defender for Office 365 feature lets you send realistic but harmless phishing emails to users and assign training to those who click?
questions.explain: Attack simulation training, a Plan 2 feature, runs benign phishing and social-engineering simulations and assigns training. Threat Explorer and Real-time detections are investigation tools, and Safe Links protects real URLs at click time.

questions.stem: Which THREE features are included in Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 but not in Plan 1? Select THREE.
questions.explain: Threat Explorer, AIR and attack simulation training are Plan 2 additions. Safe Links and Safe Attachments are already in Plan 1, so they are in both plans.

questions.stem: With Defender for Office 365 Plan 2, a security analyst wants to search all malicious emails delivered during the past week, filter by sender and URL, and soft delete them from mailboxes. Which tool should be used?
questions.explain: Threat Explorer is the Plan 2 tool for hunting and remediating email threats, including soft delete. Message trace only follows mail flow, Content explorer is a Purview data classification tool, and Real-time detections is the Plan 1 view without these remediation actions.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Microsoft 365 E5 includes Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2.
The Campaigns view groups related malicious messages into one coordinated attack view.
Zero-hour auto purge (ZAP) for email is available only with Defender for Office 365 Plan 2.

questions.explain: Microsoft 365 E5 includes Plan 2. Campaigns, a Plan 2 feature, groups related messages into a coordinated campaign. ZAP for email is part of Exchange Online Protection, so every cloud mailbox gets it.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Defender for Endpoint capability records device behaviour and detects advanced attacks in near real time so analysts can investigate process trees and timelines?
questions.explain: EDR captures detailed behavioural data, detects advanced attacks and supports investigation. ASR rules and device control are preventive controls that block behaviours or devices, and Intune compliance policies are device management, not threat detection.

questions.stem: Which TWO are attack surface reduction capabilities in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint? Select TWO.
questions.explain: Controlled folder access (ransomware protection) and network protection belong to attack surface reduction, along with ASR rules and exploit protection. Live response is a response action, advanced hunting is a query tool, and threat analytics provides threat reports.

questions.case: Tailspin Toys licenses Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 1. Antivirus and ASR rules are working, but the SOC says it can't see detailed behavioural timelines of compromised devices and wants alerts investigated and remediated automatically.
questions.stem: What should Tailspin Toys do?
options: Enable Safe Attachments for SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams
Deploy Microsoft Defender for Identity sensors on all laptops
Turn on cloud-delivered protection in Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Upgrade to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2
questions.explain: EDR and automated investigation and remediation are Plan 2 capabilities. Cloud-delivered protection improves antivirus but adds no EDR. Defender for Identity sensors go on domain controllers and identity servers, and Safe Attachments protects files in collaboration services.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to show how Microsoft Defender for Endpoint detects and contains ransomware on a laptop.
options: Onboard the device to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
EDR detects suspicious encryption behaviour and raises an alert
The analyst opens the alert and confirms ransomware from the process tree
Based on that confirmation, the analyst isolates the device from the network
questions.explain: The sensor must be onboarded before it can report. EDR then raises an alert, the analyst confirms the threat from the evidence, and that confirmation drives isolation, which contains the device while keeping its connection to the Defender service.

questions.stem: An analyst needs to stop a compromised workstation from communicating with other devices while still being able to investigate it from the Microsoft Defender portal. Which response action should they use?
options: Add a file indicator to allow the file
questions.explain: Isolate device cuts the machine off the network but keeps its connection to the Defender service, so investigation continues. A scan or an investigation package doesn't stop network traffic, and an allow indicator would permit, not block, a file.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft service acts as a cloud access security broker (CASB)?
questions.explain: Defender for Cloud Apps is Microsoft's CASB for SaaS apps. Defender for Identity protects on-premises Active Directory, Defender for Cloud covers posture and workload protection for cloud infrastructure, and Azure Firewall filters network traffic in Azure.

questions.stem: You want to find and control shadow IT with Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps. Put the steps in order.
options: Feed traffic logs or Defender for Endpoint signals into Cloud Discovery
Review the discovered apps and their risk scores from the cloud app catalog
Block the unsanctioned apps on managed devices
questions.explain: Cloud Discovery needs data first (logs or Defender for Endpoint integration). Then you assess discovered apps by risk score, mark risky ones unsanctioned, and enforce the decision by blocking them, for example on devices onboarded to Defender for Endpoint.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Cloud Discovery can use firewall and proxy traffic logs to identify cloud apps in use.
Every discovered app gets a risk score based on information in the cloud app catalog.
App connectors require installing an agent inside each SaaS application.

questions.explain: Cloud Discovery analyses traffic logs (and Defender for Endpoint data), and the cloud app catalog rates each app's risk. App connectors use the SaaS provider's APIs, so no agent is installed in the app.

questions.case: Northwind lets contractors use personal, unmanaged laptops to work in Salesforce and SharePoint Online through a browser. Security wants contractors to keep viewing documents but block them downloading any file labelled Confidential, in real time, without blocking access to the apps.
questions.stem: What should Northwind use?
options: A Defender for Cloud Apps session policy through Conditional Access App Control
Cloud Discovery with the app tagged as unsanctioned
A Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy that blocks access from unmanaged devices
An Azure network security group that denies outbound HTTPS
questions.explain: Conditional Access App Control routes the session through Defender for Cloud Apps, where a session policy can block downloads in real time while keeping access. Unsanctioning or blocking access stops all use, and an NSG works at the network layer of Azure resources.

questions.stem: Which THREE are pillars of the cloud access security broker (CASB) framework used by Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps? Select THREE.
questions.explain: The CASB framework has four pillars: visibility, data security, threat protection and compliance. Key management is an Azure Key Vault function, and identity federation is an identity provider capability, not a CASB pillar.

questions.stem: An administrator finds that a third-party OAuth app has been granted broad permissions to read all users' mail through Microsoft Graph and is behaving unusually. Which Defender for Cloud Apps capability is designed to detect and control this?
questions.explain: App governance monitors OAuth-enabled apps, their permissions and behaviour, and can disable risky ones. Cloud Discovery finds apps from traffic, Conditional Access App Control controls user sessions, and SSPM reports SaaS configuration weaknesses.

questions.stem: Where are Microsoft Defender for Identity sensors primarily installed?
questions.explain: Defender for Identity sensors run on domain controllers, and also on AD FS, AD CS and Microsoft Entra Connect servers, where they read traffic and events. Workstations are covered by Defender for Endpoint, and Exchange Online and Azure gateways do not host the sensor.

questions.case: Adatum runs a hybrid environment. Its security team suspects an attacker obtained the KRBTGT account hash and is forging Kerberos tickets to access servers across the on-premises domain.
questions.stem: Which solution is designed to detect this activity?
questions.explain: Forged Kerberos tickets using the KRBTGT key is a Golden Ticket attack against on-premises Active Directory, which Defender for Identity detects. Entra ID Protection evaluates cloud sign-in and user risk, Cloud Apps monitors SaaS, and Insider Risk Management targets risky insider data activity.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Defender for Identity, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Defender for Identity can show lateral movement paths an attacker could use to reach sensitive accounts.
Defender for Identity is managed in the Microsoft Purview portal.
Defender for Identity can detect reconnaissance such as LDAP enumeration of users and groups.

questions.explain: Lateral movement paths are a key Defender for Identity posture feature, and reconnaissance (user, group and LDAP enumeration) is a detection category. It is managed in the Microsoft Defender portal, not the Purview portal.

questions.stem: Which TWO attacks are typically detected by Microsoft Defender for Identity? Select TWO.
options: A malicious macro in an email attachment
A pass-the-hash attempt against an on-premises server
A user downloading an unusually large number of files from Box
DCSync replication requests from a non-domain-controller computer
questions.explain: Pass-the-hash (lateral movement) and DCSync (domain dominance) are on-premises AD attacks that Defender for Identity detects. Malicious attachments are handled by Defender for Office 365, and mass download from a SaaS app is a Defender for Cloud Apps anomaly.

questions.stem: Which solution continuously discovers devices and software, assesses vulnerabilities and misconfigurations, and prioritizes them by risk?
questions.explain: Defender Vulnerability Management provides continuous, sensor-based discovery, assessment and risk-based prioritisation. Cloud Apps covers SaaS usage, Compliance Manager tracks regulatory compliance, and Entra ID Protection assesses identity risk.

questions.case: Litware has Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 on its Windows laptops. It can see vulnerable software in the inventory but now also wants to block known-vulnerable app versions from running and assess browser extensions and digital certificates.
questions.stem: What does Litware need?
options: The Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management add-on
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps app governance
questions.explain: Blocking vulnerable applications, browser extension assessment and digital certificate assessment are premium capabilities in the Defender Vulnerability Management add-on (or standalone). Plan 1 has fewer features than Plan 2, and the other products don't assess endpoints.

questions.stem: Put the stages of Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management in order.
options: Prioritize by risk and threat context
questions.explain: You can only assess what you have discovered, then rank weaknesses by risk (for example, whether they are exploited in the wild), and finally remediate through remediation requests and track progress.

questions.stem: In advanced hunting, you want to see how many devices are affected by each critical vulnerability. Complete the query.
questions.code:
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where VulnerabilitySeverityLevel == "Critical"
| ____ AffectedDevices = dcount(DeviceName) by CveId
| sort by AffectedDevices desc
questions.explain: summarize with dcount() counts distinct devices per CVE. where filters rows, project selects columns, and take returns a number of rows; none of them support an aggregation with by.

questions.stem: In the Microsoft Defender portal, which feature provides reports from Microsoft security researchers on active threat actors and campaigns, including your impacted assets and recommended mitigations?
questions.explain: Threat analytics delivers researcher-written threat reports with related incidents, impacted assets and recommended actions. Activity explorer is a Purview data-activity tool, Secure Score measures posture, and the Action center tracks remediation actions.

questions.stem: A threat report names an actor "Storm-1234". In Microsoft's threat actor naming taxonomy, what does the Storm- prefix with a number indicate?
options: An emerging or developing threat group
questions.explain: Storm- followed by a number marks a newly identified or developing group that hasn't yet been given a full name. Russian state actors use Blizzard, financially motivated groups use Tempest, and private-sector offensive actors use Tsunami.

questions.stem: Which TWO types of information does a threat analytics report in the Microsoft Defender portal include? Select TWO.
options: Your organization's compliance score for ISO 27001
Assets in your organization impacted by the threat
Retention labels applied to affected documents
questions.explain: Threat analytics reports combine Microsoft research with your own data: related incidents, impacted assets, exposure and recommended mitigations. Compliance scores come from Compliance Manager and retention labels from Microsoft Purview records management.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft threat intelligence, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Threat intelligence indicators such as IPs, domains and file hashes can be matched against logs in Microsoft Sentinel.
Threat analytics reports describe threats in general only and never show which of your own assets are affected.
Threat intelligence capabilities are available to analysts inside the Microsoft Defender portal.

questions.explain: Sentinel can import TI indicators and match them with threat intelligence analytics rules. Threat analytics reports show impacted assets and related incidents in your environment. TI, including the converged Defender Threat Intelligence experience, is available in the Defender portal.

questions.stem: Which portal does a SOC use as the single place to manage Microsoft Defender XDR incidents, advanced hunting and Microsoft Sentinel?
questions.explain: The Microsoft Defender portal (security.microsoft.com) unifies Defender XDR and Sentinel. The Purview portal handles compliance and data protection, the Entra admin center manages identities, and the Intune admin center manages devices and apps.

questions.stem: A CISO asks for one number in the Microsoft Defender portal that reflects the organization's security posture across identities, devices and apps, with a list of improvement actions. What should you show?
questions.explain: Microsoft Secure Score measures security posture with recommended improvement actions across workloads. Compliance score is a Compliance Manager metric in Purview, exposure score is device-focused vulnerability exposure, and incident severity rates individual incidents.

questions.stem: Which TWO tasks would you perform in the Microsoft Defender portal rather than the Microsoft Purview portal? Select TWO.
options: Run advanced hunting queries across endpoint and email data
Create retention labels for records management
questions.explain: Advanced hunting and threat analytics are security operations features in the Defender portal. Sensitivity labels and retention labels are data protection and governance features managed in the Microsoft Purview portal.

questions.stem: A compliance officer needs to download Microsoft's latest independent SOC 2 Type 2 audit report for Microsoft 365. Where should she go?
options: Microsoft Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance dashboard
questions.explain: The Service Trust Portal publishes Microsoft's third-party audit reports, such as SOC and ISO. Compliance Manager tracks your own controls, Purview Audit logs tenant activity, and Defender for Cloud assesses your Azure resources. None of them hosts Microsoft's audit reports.

questions.stem: A user signs in to the Service Trust Portal but can't open anything under Restricted Documents. Which role assignment would give them access?
questions.explain: Restricted Documents are limited to users with roles such as Tenant Admin, Compliance Administrator, Security Administrator or Security Reader. Billing, Helpdesk and Reports Reader roles don't grant access to restricted compliance material.

questions.stem: For each statement about the Service Trust Portal, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Some audit reports and whitepapers can be viewed without signing in.
Most other documents require signing in with a Microsoft Entra work account and accepting a non-disclosure agreement.
Downloading Microsoft's ISO/IEC 27001 certificate makes your own organization ISO/IEC 27001 compliant.

questions.explain: Some STP content is public, but most documents need an Entra sign-in and acceptance of the NDA for compliance materials. The STP proves Microsoft's controls. Your own compliance still depends on the controls you implement.

questions.stem: An auditor wants an email every time Microsoft publishes a new version of an Azure SOC report she relies on. What should she do?
options: Subscribe to the Microsoft 365 admin center Message center
Create an alert policy in Microsoft Purview
Save the report to My Library in the Service Trust Portal and configure Notification Settings
Add the report as evidence to a Compliance Manager improvement action
questions.explain: Saving a document to My Library subscribes you to its series, and Notification Settings sends update emails. Message center covers service changes, not STP documents. Purview alert policies monitor tenant activity, and Compliance Manager evidence doesn't notify you of new report versions.

questions.stem: A hospital's risk team wants Microsoft guidance written specifically for healthcare and life sciences organizations. Which Service Trust Portal section is designed for this?
questions.explain: Industry and Regional Resources groups material by sector, such as healthcare and life sciences or financial services, and by region. Certifications holds audit reports, the Reports section holds general whitepapers, and My Download History only lists your past downloads.

questions.stem: Which TWO types of content can you obtain from the Service Trust Portal? Select TWO.
options: Summaries of penetration tests and security assessments of Microsoft cloud services
Your tenant's unified audit log records
ISO/IEC and SOC audit reports for Microsoft cloud services
Your organization's DLP policy match reports
Sensitivity label usage from activity explorer
questions.explain: The STP publishes evidence about Microsoft's services, such as pen-test and assessment summaries and certification audit reports. Audit logs, DLP reports and activity explorer data describe your own tenant, and you view them in the Microsoft Purview portal.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the Microsoft privacy principle 'You control your data'?
options: Microsoft may use customer data for advertising unless the customer opts out.
Your data belongs to you. You can access, modify or delete it, and Microsoft uses it only to provide the services you chose.
Customers must always manage their own encryption keys in Azure Key Vault.
Microsoft stores all customer data only in the customer's own datacenter.
questions.explain: The control principle says the data is yours to access, change or delete, and Microsoft uses it only to deliver the agreed services. Microsoft doesn't use customer data for advertising. Customer-managed keys are optional, and cloud data lives in Microsoft datacenters in the regions you choose.

questions.stem: A government agency asks Microsoft directly for a commercial customer's mailbox content. In line with Microsoft's privacy principles, what does Microsoft try to do first?
options: Redirect the agency to request the data from the customer, and notify the customer where legally permitted
Hand over the data and notify the customer afterwards
Delete the requested data to protect the customer
Give the agency read-only access through a dedicated government portal
questions.explain: Under 'Microsoft defends your data', Microsoft redirects requests to the customer, notifies the customer when the law allows, and challenges requests where it lawfully can. It doesn't give any government direct access, and it doesn't delete customer data to avoid a request.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft's privacy principles, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Microsoft mines customer data in its commercial cloud services to target advertising.
Customers can choose where their data is stored in services such as Microsoft 365 and Azure.
Microsoft encrypts customer data both at rest and in transit, for example using TLS for data in transit.

questions.explain: Microsoft commits not to use customer data for advertising or marketing research. The data location principle offers residency choices. The security principle covers encryption at rest (up to AES-256) and in transit (TLS and IPsec).

questions.case: Fabrikam, a German insurer, is moving to Microsoft 365. Its works council insists that customer records must be stored within the European Union and wants to understand which of Microsoft's privacy commitments covers this concern before approving the project.
questions.stem: Which Microsoft privacy principle addresses the works council's concern most directly?
options: Your data is secured at rest and in transit
Know where your data is located
questions.explain: The concern is where the data is stored, which is the data location principle and its residency options. Defense is about government requests, security is about encryption, and control is about who owns and uses the data.

questions.stem: Which URL opens the Microsoft Purview portal, where you manage Purview data security, data governance, and risk and compliance solutions?
questions.explain: The Microsoft Purview portal is at purview.microsoft.com. security.microsoft.com is the Microsoft Defender portal, entra.microsoft.com is the Entra admin center for identity, and portal.azure.com manages Azure resources.

questions.stem: Two admins in the same tenant open the Microsoft Purview portal. One sees the Insider Risk Management solution card and the other doesn't. What is the most likely reason?
options: Insider Risk Management is available only in the Microsoft Defender portal.
The Knowledge Center hides solutions the admin hasn't completed training for.
The admin's portal theme setting hides some solution cards.
The solutions shown depend on the user's role permissions and the organization's licensing.
questions.explain: The Purview portal only shows solution cards you have permissions and a subscription for, so role differences explain it. Insider Risk Management is a Purview solution. The Knowledge Center is learning content, and themes only change appearance.

questions.stem: For each statement about the Microsoft Purview portal, select Yes if true.

statements.s: It brings data security, data governance, and risk and compliance solutions together in one experience.
The home page's Compliance posture status card shows information from Compliance Manager.
The Microsoft Purview compliance portal at compliance.microsoft.com remains the main portal for Purview solutions.

questions.explain: The Purview portal unifies data security, data governance and compliance, and its Compliance posture status card links to Compliance Manager. The older Microsoft Purview compliance portal has been retired, and its features moved to the new portal.

questions.stem: In Compliance Manager, which type of control is implemented entirely by Microsoft for its cloud services?
questions.explain: Microsoft-managed controls are implemented by Microsoft, and you can see their implementation details and audit results. Customer-managed controls are yours, and shared controls are split between you and Microsoft. 'Custom' describes templates you build, not who is responsible for a control.

questions.stem: Your organization must track its progress toward ISO/IEC 27001 for Microsoft 365. What should you create in Compliance Manager?
options: An assessment based on the ISO/IEC 27001 regulation template
A sensitivity label policy scoped to ISO documents
An auto-apply retention label policy for audit evidence
questions.explain: Assessments created from regulation templates group the controls and improvement actions for a standard and score your progress. Label, retention and insider risk policies protect or govern data, but they don't measure compliance against a regulation.

questions.stem: Which THREE are key elements of Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager? Select THREE.
questions.explain: Compliance Manager is built from regulation templates, assessments, controls and improvement actions. Review sets belong to eDiscovery, and trainable classifiers belong to data classification.

questions.stem: You need to start tracking compliance with a new regulation in Compliance Manager. Put the steps in order.
options: Create an assessment from the template
Review the assessment's controls and improvement actions
Implement and test the improvement actions
questions.explain: The template defines the regulation and the assessment applies it to your services. The controls lead to improvement actions, which you implement and test (manually or automatically). Points then show up in the assessment score.

questions.stem: In Compliance Manager, what is an improvement action called if you implement it by changing a configuration in a solution, such as enabling a DLP policy?
questions.explain: Technical actions are done by working with the technology, for example a configuration change. Documentation and operational actions are the two kinds of nontechnical action. 'Corrective' is a risk category used for scoring, not an implementation type.

questions.stem: Your team meets a Compliance Manager improvement action's requirement with a non-Microsoft security tool instead of the recommended Microsoft feature. Which implementation status should you set?
questions.explain: Alternative implementation records that you met the requirement with other tools or methods than Microsoft recommends. Out of scope means the action doesn't apply and earns no points. Planned means it isn't done yet, and Implemented means you followed the recommended approach.

questions.stem: For each statement about Compliance Manager improvement actions, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Automatic testing is turned on by default for eligible improvement actions.
Compliance Manager can use Microsoft Defender for Cloud signals to test actions for Azure, AWS and Google Cloud resources.
Evidence attached to an action with test status Passed can still be deleted by any user with read access.

questions.explain: Automatic testing is on by default, and Defender for Cloud gives multicloud signals. Read-only users can only view evidence. After an action's status is Passed, Failed or Out of scope, its evidence can't be deleted at all.

questions.stem: An improvement action requires your organization to write and publish an acceptable use policy for staff. How does Compliance Manager classify this action?
questions.explain: Writing a policy document is a nontechnical documentation action. Operational actions are about running processes, such as training or reviews. Technical actions change a configuration, and Microsoft-managed actions are Microsoft's responsibility, not your HR policy.

questions.stem: What is a new organization's initial compliance score in Compliance Manager based on?
options: The number of DLP alerts in the last 30 days
The number of published sensitivity labels
The Microsoft 365 Data Protection Baseline assessment
questions.explain: Every tenant starts with the default Microsoft 365 Data Protection Baseline assessment, and its controls produce the initial score. Secure Score is a separate security posture measure. Alert counts and label counts aren't the basis of the score.

questions.stem: Which type of improvement action adds the most points to your compliance score when completed?
questions.explain: Preventative mandatory actions are worth 27 points, the highest value. Preventative discretionary actions are worth 9, detective and corrective mandatory actions 3, and detective and corrective discretionary actions 1. The weighting reflects how much risk each action reduces.

questions.stem: For each statement about compliance score, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A compliance score of 100% guarantees that your organization complies with the regulation.
A mandatory action earns more points than a discretionary action in the same risk category.
Compliance score and Microsoft Secure Score measure the same thing.

questions.explain: Compliance score helps you track and prioritize, but Microsoft says it isn't a guarantee of compliance. Mandatory actions are weighted higher, for example 27 versus 9 for preventative actions. Secure Score measures security posture, not regulatory compliance.

questions.case: Lena manages three Compliance Manager assessments: the Data Protection Baseline, ISO/IEC 27001 and NIST CSF. She presents the overall compliance score to leadership, and the CFO notices that it doesn't equal the average of the three assessment scores. He asks whether the dashboard is broken.
questions.stem: Which explanation should Lena give?
options: Assessment scores never include Microsoft-managed actions, but the overall score does.
The overall score only reflects the Data Protection Baseline assessment.
In the overall score, each Microsoft-managed and technical action counts once, while nontechnical actions count once per group.
Assessment scores refresh weekly, while the overall score refreshes hourly.
questions.explain: Actions shared across assessments are counted differently in the overall score. Microsoft-managed and technical actions count once, and nontechnical actions count once per group, so it isn't a simple average. Assessment scores do include Microsoft-managed actions, and statuses refresh about every 24 hours.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Purview classification method detects credit card numbers by using a pattern, a checksum and nearby keywords?
questions.explain: Sensitive information types match patterns with supporting evidence such as checksums and keywords, and report a confidence level. Trainable classifiers use machine learning on example content. Sensitivity and retention labels are what you apply after classification. They don't detect content themselves.

questions.stem: A bank wants DLP to match only its real customer account numbers, taken from a database export, so that look-alike numbers don't cause false positives. Which classification method fits best?
options: Exact data match (EDM) sensitive information type
questions.explain: EDM matches the actual values from your own sensitive data table, which keeps false positives very low. Named entities detect generic names, addresses and medical terms. Pretrained classifiers recognize document categories, and fingerprinting recognizes forms built from a template.

questions.stem: The legal team wants Purview to detect any completed copy of the company's standard nondisclosure agreement form, no matter what has been filled in. Which feature should you use?
options: Keyword dictionary in a custom SIT
questions.explain: Document fingerprinting creates a sensitive information type from a template, so it recognizes filled-in variations of that form. EDM needs a table of exact values, named entities detect people, places and medical terms, and a keyword dictionary would miss the form's structure or match unrelated documents.

questions.stem: What best describes how trainable classifiers differ from sensitive information types?
options: They only work for Exchange Online email.
They encrypt content as soon as it's classified.
They use machine learning to recognize a category of content, such as resumes or source code, rather than a fixed pattern.
They must be applied manually by users in Office apps.
questions.explain: Trainable classifiers learn from examples to recognize kinds of content that have no fixed pattern. They work across many locations and don't encrypt anything (labels do that). They're applied automatically in policies, not chosen by users.

questions.stem: Which TWO Microsoft Purview features can use trainable classifiers as a condition? Select TWO.
questions.explain: DLP policies and auto-apply retention label policies (as well as sensitivity auto-labeling and communication compliance) can use trainable classifiers. Role groups control permissions, audit retention policies filter by service, activity or user, and STP notifications are about document updates.

questions.stem: For each statement about data classification in Microsoft Purview, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Microsoft provides pretrained trainable classifiers that are ready to use.
Named entity SITs can detect items such as person names and physical addresses.
You create a custom trainable classifier by writing a regular expression.

questions.explain: Pretrained classifiers are available out of the box, and named entities use dictionaries and patterns for names, addresses and medical terms. You train a custom classifier by giving it sample content. Regular expressions define custom sensitive information types.

questions.stem: Which Purview tool shows a current snapshot of items that have sensitivity labels, retention labels or sensitive information types, and where those items are stored?
questions.explain: Content explorer shows what exists now and where, with drill-down to individual items. Activity explorer shows actions taken over time. Audit searches activity logs, and Compliance Manager tracks regulatory controls.

questions.case: Amir is a Compliance Administrator at Northwind. He can open the Content explorer tab, but the list of items is empty for him. His manager wants him to see which items match each sensitive information type and where they're stored. He must not be able to open or read the files' contents.
questions.stem: Which role group should you add Amir to?
questions.explain: Content Explorer List Viewer lets you see items and their locations in list view. Viewing item contents needs the separate Content Explorer Content Viewer group. Admin and reader roles open the tab but don't show the list, and eDiscovery Manager is for eDiscovery cases.

questions.stem: Which Purview tool gives a historical view of actions on labeled content, such as 'label applied', 'label changed' and 'file read'?
questions.explain: Activity explorer shows labeling, DLP and endpoint activities over time, using data from the unified audit log. Content explorer is a current inventory of items. Data Map catalogs data estate metadata, and compliance score measures regulatory progress.

questions.stem: For each statement about activity explorer, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Activity explorer reports on up to 30 days of data.
Activity explorer data comes from the Microsoft 365 unified audit log.
Activities in core services such as SharePoint appear in activity explorer in real time.

questions.explain: Activity explorer covers up to 30 days and uses the unified audit log. It isn't real time: Microsoft says to allow about 60–90 minutes for Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams activity to appear.

questions.stem: A security lead is choosing between content explorer and activity explorer. Which TWO questions can activity explorer answer? Select TWO.
options: Which user downgraded the sensitivity label on a file last week?
How many SharePoint files currently contain credit card numbers?
Which DLP rule matched when a user copied a file to a USB drive?
Which regulations the tenant is being assessed against
Which version of Microsoft's SOC report is current
questions.explain: Activity explorer records actions such as label changes and Endpoint DLP rule matches over time. A count of files containing card numbers right now is content explorer's job. Regulations are tracked in Compliance Manager, and SOC reports are in the Service Trust Portal.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Purview feature can classify a document and encrypt it so only specific people can open it, with the protection staying on the file wherever it goes?
questions.explain: Sensitivity labels classify content and can apply encryption and content markings that persist with the item. Retention labels only keep or delete content. DLP enforces sharing rules but doesn't travel with the file, and Data Map catalogs data estate metadata.

questions.stem: For each statement about sensitivity labels, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A single document can have two sensitivity labels applied at the same time.
A document can have a sensitivity label and a retention label at the same time.
Sensitivity labels can be applied to Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 Groups and SharePoint sites to control privacy and external sharing.

questions.explain: Each item can have only one sensitivity label, but it can also have a retention label. Container labels on teams, groups and sites control settings such as privacy and external sharing. They don't label the files stored inside.

questions.stem: Which TWO actions can a sensitivity label perform on a Word document? Select TWO.
options: Add a header, footer or watermark
Delete the document after seven years
Encrypt the document to restrict who can open it
Place the document on eDiscovery hold
Declare the document a regulatory record
questions.explain: Sensitivity labels apply content markings and encryption. Deleting after a period and declaring records are done with retention labels. Holds are placed through eDiscovery cases.

questions.stem: You need every user to choose a sensitivity label before they can save a new document or send an email. Where do you configure this?
options: In the encryption settings of each sensitivity label
In the sensitivity label policy, by enabling mandatory labeling
questions.explain: Mandatory labeling is a label policy setting, like default labels and downgrade justification. Encryption is a setting on the label itself. DLP rules can block sharing but can't force users to label, and Compliance Manager only tracks actions.

questions.stem: You're rolling out sensitivity labels for the first time. Put the steps in order.
options: Define the labels and their protection settings
Publish the labels to users and groups in a label policy
Users apply labels in Office apps
questions.explain: You create labels (with encryption and marking settings) first. They do nothing until a label policy publishes them to users or groups. Users then apply them in apps, and activity explorer shows label activity so you can tune the rollout.

questions.case: Contoso has four sensitivity labels: Public, General, Confidential and Highly Confidential. A user opens a Highly Confidential file and tries to change its label to General. The label policy uses the default justification setting.
questions.stem: What happens?
options: The change is blocked, because labels can never be lowered.
The user is prompted to give a justification, because General has a lower priority than Highly Confidential.
The file keeps both labels, and the higher one takes effect.
The change succeeds silently, because users can always change labels.
questions.explain: Lowering a label to a lower-priority one requires a justification by default, and the reason is recorded (it can be reviewed in activity explorer). Downgrades aren't blocked outright. An item can only have one sensitivity label.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Purview solution detects sensitive information in emails and documents and can block them from being shared outside the organization?
questions.explain: DLP policies inspect content against conditions such as SITs and act on it, for example by blocking or warning. Insider risk management detects risky behavior patterns, records management keeps records unchanged, and Compliance Manager tracks regulatory progress.

questions.stem: In a DLP policy, what is the in-app notification that warns users their action might share sensitive data inappropriately?
questions.explain: Policy tips warn users inside apps such as Outlook and can let them override with a justification. Alerts go to admins. Disposition reviews are part of records management, and legal hold notifications are part of eDiscovery.

questions.stem: Microsoft recommends a staged approach to deploying a DLP policy. Put the steps in order.
options: Design the policy from your control objectives
Run the policy in simulation mode
Monitor outcomes and fine-tune the policy
Turn on the policy to enforce actions
questions.explain: You design first, then simulate. Simulation mode evaluates the policy without enforcing actions. You then monitor and fine-tune to reduce false positives and business disruption, and only after that enable enforcement.

questions.stem: You're creating a DLP policy in Security & Compliance PowerShell. It must run in simulation, with no enforcement actions, but still send notifications to users. Complete the command.
questions.explain: -Mode TestWithNotifications runs the policy in simulation and still sends notifications. TestWithoutNotifications sends none. Enable enforces the policy's actions. AuditOnly isn't a valid -Mode value.

questions.case: Tailwind Traders wants staff to be able to email a single customer credit card number to a partner, but they should be warned first. If an email contains 10 or more card numbers, it should be blocked unless the sender gives a business justification.
questions.stem: What should you configure?
options: Two sensitivity labels with different encryption settings
A communication compliance policy with two reviewers
An insider risk management policy using the Data leaks template
A DLP policy with two rules: a low-volume rule with a policy tip, and a high-volume rule that blocks with override
questions.explain: DLP rules combine conditions, such as the number of SIT instances, with actions such as policy tips and block with override. Labels encrypt but don't count card numbers in outbound mail. Communication compliance and insider risk detect and review behavior; neither blocks the email in real time.

questions.stem: You must stop users copying files that contain sensitive information to USB drives from their Windows 11 laptops. Which solution should you use?
questions.explain: Endpoint DLP enforces DLP on onboarded Windows and macOS devices. It can audit or block copying to removable media, printing and uploads. Retention keeps content, container labels control sites and teams, and Conditional Access controls sign-in to apps, not file copies.

questions.stem: Which THREE user activities can Endpoint DLP audit or restrict on onboarded devices? Select THREE.
options: Copying a sensitive file to a removable USB device
Signing in from an unfamiliar location
Copying sensitive content to the clipboard
questions.explain: Endpoint DLP monitors device activities such as printing, copying to USB or network shares, copying to the clipboard and access by unallowed apps. Risky sign-in locations are Entra ID Protection signals, and password resets are an identity function (SSPR).

questions.stem: Your organization must keep certain financial documents unchanged for 10 years and then have someone approve their deletion. Which Microsoft Purview solution is designed for this?
questions.explain: Records management uses retention labels to declare records, which locks them against edits and deletion, and supports disposition review with proof of disposal. DLP prevents data leaks, Information Protection classifies and encrypts, and communication compliance reviews messages.

questions.stem: Which item status means that nobody, not even a Global Administrator, can remove the label, edit the item, or shorten the retention period?
questions.explain: A regulatory record is the strictest option. Its label can't be removed by anyone, edits and moves are blocked, and the retention period can only be made longer. Container admins can still remove the label from a locked record. A Highly Confidential sensitivity label protects access but doesn't prevent deletion.

questions.stem: The option to mark content as a regulatory record isn't visible in retention label settings by default. Complete the Security & Compliance PowerShell command that makes it appear.
questions.explain: Set-RegulatoryComplianceUI -Enabled $true shows the regulatory record option. Because it's so restrictive and irreversible, it's hidden by default. Set-ComplianceTag modifies existing labels, Set-RetentionCompliancePolicy modifies policies, and Enable-RegulatoryRecord isn't a real cmdlet.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Purview Records Management, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Event-based retention can start the retention period when an event occurs, such as an employee leaving.
Items are declared as records by applying a sensitivity label.
Disposition review lets reviewers approve deletion at the end of the retention period and keeps proof of disposal.

questions.explain: Event-based retention and disposition review with proof of disposal are core Records Management features. Records are declared with retention labels. Sensitivity labels handle classification and protection.

questions.stem: You must keep all Microsoft Teams chat and channel messages for three years. What should you use?
options: A retention label policy published to Teams
A retention policy that includes the Teams locations
A sensitivity label applied to each team
questions.explain: Teams messages support retention policies but not retention labels, so label policies (manual or auto-apply) don't work for them. Sensitivity labels on a team control privacy and sharing, not retention.

questions.case: Woodgrove Bank has two retention policies that both include the same SharePoint site. Policy A keeps content for 7 years. Policy B deletes content after 3 years. A user deletes a document from the site in year 2.
questions.stem: What happens to the document?
options: It's kept (in the Preservation Hold library) until the 7-year period ends, because retention wins over deletion.
It's permanently deleted at year 3, because the shortest deletion period wins.
It's permanently deleted straight away, because the user deleted it.
The policies cancel each other out, and normal recycle bin behavior applies.
questions.explain: Under the principles of retention, retention wins over deletion and the longest retention period wins. The deleted item is kept in the hidden Preservation Hold library for the full 7 years. 'Shortest deletion period wins' only applies after the retention rules are resolved.

questions.stem: You're creating a retention policy in Security & Compliance PowerShell for the Finance SharePoint site. (A retention rule will be added afterwards.) Complete the command.
questions.explain: -SharePointLocation takes SharePoint site URLs (or All). -ExchangeLocation is for mailboxes, -OneDriveLocation for OneDrive accounts, and -ModernGroupLocation for Microsoft 365 Groups. The policy isn't valid until a retention rule is added.

questions.stem: Which TWO requirements can be met with a retention label but NOT with a retention policy? Select TWO.
options: Declare an individual document a record
Retain all email in every mailbox for 5 years
Trigger a disposition review at the end of the retention period
Apply settings to an entire SharePoint site
questions.explain: Only retention labels can declare records and trigger disposition review. Blanket rules for all mailboxes or a whole site are best done with retention policies, and Teams messages support only retention policies.

questions.stem: You need a retention label that keeps contracts for 7 years from creation and then deletes them automatically. Complete the Security & Compliance PowerShell command.
questions.explain: KeepAndDelete keeps content for the duration and then deletes it. Keep only retains it, and Delete only deletes after the period. RetainThenDelete matches the portal wording but isn't a valid -RetentionAction value.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Purview capability scans data sources such as Azure SQL Database and on-premises SQL Server to capture metadata, classifications and data lineage?
questions.explain: Data Map scans registered sources across on-premises, Azure, multicloud and SaaS, and builds an inventory of assets, classifications and lineage. Content explorer shows labeled and SIT-matching items in Microsoft 365. Compliance Manager tracks regulations, and Audit records activity.

questions.stem: A data steward wants to group curated tables and Power BI reports into one discoverable package so analysts can find it and request access. Which Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog feature fits?
questions.explain: A data product bundles related assets for a use case so people can find them and request access. A governance domain is the business boundary that contains data products. A glossary term defines business vocabulary, and a retention label has nothing to do with the catalog.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Purview solution correlates signals such as mass file downloads and an upcoming resignation date to detect possible data theft by an employee?
questions.explain: Insider risk management correlates user activity with signals such as HR resignation dates to detect risky behavior from insiders. Entra ID Protection detects compromised identities. DLP enforces rules on individual content actions, and Defender for Cloud Apps governs SaaS app usage.

questions.stem: You plan to use the 'Data theft by departing users' insider risk policy template. You want it to be triggered by resignation and termination dates from your HR system. What should you configure?
options: An eDiscovery hold on all mailboxes
questions.explain: The Microsoft 365 HR connector imports resignation and termination dates that trigger the policy (without it, the template can instead trigger on Microsoft Entra account deletion). Sentinel connectors feed a SIEM, holds preserve content for legal cases, and Compliance Manager assessments track regulations.

questions.stem: Put the stages of the insider risk management workflow in order.
options: Create a policy from a template
Alerts are generated when activity matches the policy
Take action, such as notifying the user or escalating
questions.explain: Policies define the users and risk indicators in scope. Matching activity creates alerts, which reviewers triage. Alerts that need deeper review become cases, and the workflow ends with an action, such as a notice to the user, resolving the case, or escalating to eDiscovery (Premium).

questions.case: Adatum's works council worries that insider risk management will let analysts snoop on named employees. The compliance lead is preparing answers.
questions.stem: For each statement about insider risk management, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Usernames are pseudonymized by default in insider risk management.
Insider risk management blocks file downloads in real time when a policy matches.
Actions taken by people assigned insider risk management roles can be reviewed in an audit log.

questions.explain: Insider risk management is built with privacy by design: users are pseudonymized by default, and role-based access and audit logs record what analysts do. It detects risk and creates alerts. Real-time blocking is done by DLP, which Adaptive Protection can tighten for risky users.

questions.stem: HR wants to detect harassing or threatening language in Microsoft Teams chats and have designated reviewers handle the matches. Which solution should you use?
options: Insider risk management with the Data leaks template
questions.explain: Communication compliance scans Teams, Exchange, Viva Engage and Copilot messages for inappropriate content, and reviewers can tag, notify or remove messages. DLP looks for sensitive data, not harassment. The Data leaks template is about leaking information, and Audit logs activity without judging message content.

questions.case: Litware wants stricter controls only for risky users. Users that insider risk management rates Elevated should be blocked from sharing sensitive files externally. Lower-risk users should only see a policy tip, and admins shouldn't have to keep updating group membership by hand.
questions.stem: What should Litware use?
options: Adaptive Protection, with DLP policies that use insider risk levels
A static retention policy scoped to risky users
Microsoft Entra ID Protection user risk policy
questions.explain: Adaptive Protection gives users an insider risk level (Minor, Moderate or Elevated) and applies DLP, Conditional Access or data lifecycle controls to them automatically. Retention doesn't block sharing. Communication compliance reviews messages, and Entra ID Protection user risk is about compromised accounts, not insider behavior.

questions.stem: During a lawsuit, legal counsel needs to make sure relevant mailbox and OneDrive content can't be permanently deleted while the case is open. What should be used?
options: A hold in an eDiscovery case
questions.explain: eDiscovery holds preserve content in its current location for the life of the case and override deletion. DLP prevents sharing, encryption controls who can open content, and audit retention policies keep log records, not the content itself.

questions.stem: Which TWO capabilities require premium eDiscovery features (for example, a Microsoft 365 E5 licence)? Select TWO.
options: Analytics such as near-duplicate detection and email threading
questions.explain: Review sets, tagging, OCR, analytics (near-duplicate detection, email threading, themes) and predictive coding are premium. Cases, holds, searches and export are standard eDiscovery features.

questions.stem: An investigator runs a compliance search from Security & Compliance PowerShell for all mailboxes that mention Project Falcon and its budget. Complete the command.
questions.code:
Connect-IPPSSession -EnableSearchOnlySession
New-ComplianceSearch -Name "Falcon" -ExchangeLocation All ____ "'Project Falcon' AND 'budget'"
Start-ComplianceSearch -Identity "Falcon"
questions.explain: -ContentMatchQuery takes the keyword or KQL query that filters the content searched. -SearchQuery belonged to the retired Search-Mailbox cmdlet. -KeywordFilter and -Query aren't New-ComplianceSearch parameters.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Purview Audit, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Audit (Standard) is enabled by default for organizations with an eligible subscription.
Audit (Standard) keeps audit records for 180 days.
Audit (Standard) lets you keep audit records for up to 10 years with custom retention policies.

questions.explain: Audit (Standard) is on by default and keeps records for 180 days. Custom audit log retention policies need Audit (Premium). Keeping records for 10 years also needs the 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on licence.

questions.case: After a suspected business email compromise, Contoso's investigators find that the activity started eight months ago. Audit (Standard) no longer has records that old. For the future, they want Exchange and SharePoint audit records kept for 1 year by default, and records for executives kept for 10 years.
questions.stem: What should Contoso implement?
options: Export Audit (Standard) results to CSV every week
Extend activity explorer retention to 1 year
Create an eDiscovery hold on the executives' mailboxes
Audit (Premium), with a custom audit log retention policy and the 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on licence for executives
questions.explain: Audit (Premium) keeps Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Entra ID records for 1 year by default. Custom audit retention policies with the 10-year add-on extend that for chosen users. Audit (Standard) keeps 180 days, activity explorer is fixed at 30 days, and holds preserve content, not audit records.

questions.stem: You need to search the unified audit log for everything a specific user did over two weeks. Complete the Exchange Online PowerShell command.
questions.explain: -UserIds filters by the UPN of the user who performed the actions, and -ResultSize allows up to 5,000 results. -Identity, -Mailbox and -UserPrincipalName aren't Search-UnifiedAuditLog parameters. StartDate and EndDate are required.
